items.title: PolicyStack
items.text:
PolicyStack keeps OpenShift cluster configuration in Git as Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management (ACM) policies. Each directory under stack/ is an element: a Helm chart that renders policies through the policy-library chart. On the hub, an Argo CD ApplicationSet creates one Application per element for each cluster that has a fleet file. Argo CD syncs the policies to the hub only, and ACM delivers each one to the single cluster it targets.

flowchart LR
  subgraph git["Git"]
    fleet["fleet/#lt;cluster#gt;.yaml<br>default branch"]
    stack["stack/#lt;element#gt;/"]
    vals["values.yaml<br>values/**"]
  end
  subgraph hub["ACM hub"]
    appset["ApplicationSet<br>policystack"]
    app["Application<br>#lt;element#gt;-#lt;cluster#gt;"]
    pol["Policies in pstack"]
  end
  spoke["Managed cluster<br>governance add-on"]
  fleet -->|"revision, valueFiles"| appset
  stack --> appset
  appset -->|"one per element × cluster"| app
  vals --> app
  app -->|"Helm render, sync"| pol
  pol -->|"Placement: one cluster"| spoke
  spoke -.->|"compliance"| pol

A fleet file pins a cluster to a Git revision and lists its values layers:

# fleet/prod-east-1.yaml
revision: main # (1)!
valueFiles: # (2)!
  - environments/prod.yaml
  - datacenters/dc1.yaml
  - platforms/aws.yaml
  1. Branch, tag or SHA. Every Application for this cluster renders from it.
  2. Files under values/, lowest precedence first. values/clusters/prod-east-1.yaml is always added last.

Tip

Add hub: <hubName> and the hub also builds the cluster with HyperShift, Hive or SiteConfig, and destroys it on state: absent. See Cluster lifecycle.

items.title: How a change reaches a cluster
items.text:
1. Commit to the revision the cluster pins. Here, turning on gitops for one cluster:

    # values/clusters/prod-east-1.yaml
 stack:
+  gitops:
+    enabled: true

    Clusters pinned to other revisions are unaffected. Fleet file edits count only on the default branch.

  2. Argo CD renders the element with the cluster's values cascade and syncs Policy, PolicySet, Placement and PlacementBinding into pstack on the hub.

  3. ACM delivers. The Placement selects only that cluster, and its governance add-on applies the policy: enforce changes the cluster, inform only reports. Compliance shows on the replicated Policy in the cluster's namespace on the hub.

items.title: Terms
items.text: Term Meaning Element A stack/<element>/ Helm chart that depends on policy-library. Its values define the policies it renders. Fleet file fleet/<cluster>.yaml, or fleet/hubs/<hubName>.yaml for the hub, on the default branch. Sets the revision, the values files and optionally the hub that builds the cluster. Hub The cluster running ACM and OpenShift GitOps. Holds the ApplicationSets, Applications, Policies and the control planes it builds. ACM manages it as local-cluster, so you give it a fleet file too, at fleet/hubs/<hubName>.yaml. Managed cluster A cluster ACM manages, imported by hand or built by a hub. The GitOpsCluster imports it into Argo CD; it gets one Application per element once it also has a fleet file. Release The Application name, also the Helm release name: <element>-<cluster>, or <element>-<hubName> on the hub. Policy and Placement names derive from it. Revision The branch, tag or SHA in a fleet file. All of the cluster's Applications render from it. Values cascade The ordered values files Helm gets for one Application. Later files override earlier ones.

items.title: Advanced Cluster Security
items.text:
Central runs on the ACM hub. Every secured cluster, the hub included, registers with one cluster registration secret (CRS) that you generate on the hub, following Red Hat's CRS procedure.

# values/acm/<hubName>.yaml
stack:
  acs:
    enabled: true
    toggles:
      central: true
      secured: true

# values/environments/<env>.yaml, or any layer every secured cluster reads
stack:
  acs:
    enabled: true
    toggles:
      secured: true

items.title: How it works
items.text:
• You generate the CRS once and apply it to stackrox on the hub as cluster-registration-secret, the name the operator reads. The hub's SecuredCluster uses it as is.
  • The secured policy copies it to stackrox/cluster-registration-secret on every other secured cluster. centralEndpoint is the host of Central's Route on the hub, port 443.
  • Each cluster uses the CRS once. Sensor then renews its own certificates, so expiring, replacing or revoking the CRS never affects a registered cluster.

Requirements

  • ACS 4.10+. CRS is Technology Preview on 4.9, which works.
  • Generating a CRS needs the Admin role.

items.title: Generate the CRS
items.text:
On the hub, once central-central-ready is Compliant:

export ROX_CENTRAL_ADDRESS=$(oc -n stackrox get route central -o jsonpath='{.spec.host}'):443
export ROX_API_TOKEN=<token with the Admin role> # (1)!
roxctl -e "$ROX_CENTRAL_ADDRESS" central crs generate fleet --valid-for 8760h --output crs.yaml
oc apply -n stackrox -f crs.yaml
rm crs.yaml
  1. Platform Configuration > Integrations > API Token. Or skip it and pass --password with the admin password from Secret stackrox/central-htpasswd.

Set --valid-for

Without it the CRS lasts 24 hours.

Anything that writes the same Secret works too, for example an ExternalSecret from your secret store.

items.title: Health
items.text:
Policy Compliant means central-crs-ready The hub holds the CRS with over 90 days left. Checked daily secured-tls The cluster holds the CRS. NonCompliant everywhere at once when the hub's copy is gone secured-agents-ready Sensor is ready. A refused or expired registration shows up here

Not detected

A cluster still holding certificates from another Central (moved to another hub, Central reinstalled with a new CA) reports ready while it is disconnected. Check Platform Configuration > Clusters.

items.title: Renew or rotate
items.text:
When central-crs-ready turns NonCompliant, run Generate the CRS again. The fleet copies follow. To revoke the old one, or after a leak, run roxctl central crs revoke <id>; the ID is on the Secret's crs.platform.stackrox.io/id annotation. Do not delete the Secret.

After a Central reinstall the CRS is no longer valid. Generate a new one.

items.title: Re-register a cluster
items.text:
Central refuses a CRS for any cluster name that has connected before.

Event Steps Rebuilt or re-created under the same name, including lifecycle state: absent then re-added; SecuredCluster or stackrox namespace deleted 1 Moved to another hub; Central reinstalled 2, 3 Central restored from backup None if sensor reconnects, else 1, 2, 3 Still refused after step 1 2, 3 Still refused after steps 2-3 1
  1. Hub: delete the cluster in Platform Configuration > Clusters, or run roxctl cluster delete --name <cluster>.
  2. Cluster: oc -n stackrox get secret -o name | grep -E '/tls-cert-|/(sensor|collector|admission-control)-tls$' | xargs oc -n stackrox delete
  3. Cluster: oc -n stackrox delete pod -l app=sensor

items.title: Migrating from init bundles
items.text:
Registered clusters keep the certificates they already have, so they never re-register.

  1. Remove stack.acs.config.bootstrapImage from every values layer. Otherwise POLICY035 fails the PR.
  2. Make sure the hub and every cluster run ACS 4.9 or later. Lift any operatorPolicies.acs.versions pin below that.
  3. Merge, then generate the CRS. Until you do, central-crs-ready and secured-tls are NonCompliant and nothing changes on the clusters.
  4. Every cluster gets cluster-registration-secret. centralEndpoint loses a trailing space the old Job wrote, so sensor rolls out once on each cluster.
  5. Wait until central-crs-ready, secured-tls and secured-agents-ready are Compliant everywhere.
  6. Optional, on the hub: oc -n stackrox delete job/create-cluster-init-bundle-v2 sa/create-cluster-init role/create-cluster-init rolebinding/create-cluster-init.

Keep the old secrets

Leave sensor-tls, collector-tls and admission-control-tls on every cluster, and let the old init bundle expire rather than revoking it. Deleting them before cluster-registration-secret exists fails sensor with InitBundleSecretsMissingError.

items.title: Clusters and Applications
items.text:
Two ApplicationSets in openshift-gitops on the hub turn fleet files into Argo CD Applications:

ApplicationSet Creates Template policystack One Application per element per cluster. Day-2 config. appset.yaml policystack-lifecycle One Application per fleet file this hub builds (Cluster lifecycle, Global Hub). lifecycle.yaml

items.title: Fleet files
items.text:
One file per cluster: fleet/<cluster>.yaml, named exactly like its ManagedCluster. The hub uses fleet/hubs/<hubName>.yaml (The hub).

Imported clusterHub-built cluster 
# fleet/prod-east-1.yaml
revision: main
channel: stable-4.20
valueFiles: # (1)!
  - environments/prod.yaml
  - datacenters/dc1.yaml
  - platforms/aws.yaml
  1. Paths under values/, lowest precedence first (Order). Any file works, so a custom layer like tenants/payments.yaml is just a file you list.
# fleet/hcp-kubevirt.yaml
revision: main
hub: acm-dc1 # (1)!
version: 4.20.8
valueFiles:
  - environments/nonprod.yaml
  - platforms/kubevirt.yaml
  1. Needs fleet/hubs/acm-dc1.yaml to exist.
Key Required Effect revision Yes Branch, tag or SHA every Application renders from (Revision). valueFiles No Values layers, lowest precedence first. hub No hubName of the hub that builds the cluster. Without it the cluster must be imported. state No present (default) or absent, which destroys the cluster (Destroy). Requires hub. install No The cluster to build (Install keys). Requires hub. version With hub OpenShift release, x.y.z. Bumping it upgrades (Upgrades). channel No Upgrade channel.

The validator enforces: no other keys, every valueFiles entry exists, and a hub file sets no hub, state or install. version and channel go only in fleet files (Upgrades). policystack ignores the lifecycle keys.

Quote numbers and booleans

Argo CD reads fleet files as YAML 1.1. revision: 1.10 pins 1.1. Write "1.10", "20261003", "on".

Fleet files are read only from the default branch (HEAD). fleet/ on other branches does nothing. Changing the default branch re-points every cluster, and a cluster with no file there loses its Applications.

Changes land within about 6 minutes (3 minute generator requeue plus 3 minute branch cache). An ApplicationSet webhook makes them immediate, except a fix for a failed generation, which waits for the 3 minute retry.

Upstream ships no live fleet files. Examples are the validator fixtures in tools/validator/testdata/clusters/.

Migrating from config.<baseDomain> labels

config.<baseDomain>/<category>.<priority>: <value> becomes <category>s/<value>.yaml, in priority order.

# config.example.com/environment.1: prod
# config.example.com/datacenter.2: dc1
valueFiles:
  - environments/prod.yaml
  - datacenters/dc1.yaml

PolicyStack reads five labels. You only ever set the last one.

Label Set by Effect clusterID ACM Selects the cluster's Argo CD secret, becomes selectedId. No label, no Applications. local-cluster ACM, on the hub Switches to the hub file (The hub). name ACM Placement selector matches it (Placement). apps.open-cluster-management.io/cluster-name ACM GitOpsCluster Matches hub to a default-mode managed hub (Lifecycle generator). global-hub.open-cluster-management.io/deploy-mode You, on Global Hub import default switches a managed hub to fleet/hubs/<cluster>.yaml (Global Hub).

items.title: Revision
items.text:
A branch (slashes work), tag or commit SHA. The Render Diff PR comment shows each cluster's Policies at its revision before and after merge.

One bad fleet file freezes this hub's fleet

If a fleet file this hub reads fails to parse, lacks revision, or pins a missing revision, policystack generation fails and no Application for any cluster is created, updated or deleted until it is fixed. A parse error stops policystack-lifecycle the same way. A bad revision there breaks only lifecycle-<cluster>.

oc get applicationset policystack -n openshift-gitops \
  -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions[?(@.type=="ErrorOccurred")].message}'

Pin tags, SHAs or protected branches. A deleted pinned branch freezes the fleet, and GitHub deletes PR branches on merge when automatic head branch deletion is on.

items.title: The hub
items.text:
The hub's ManagedCluster has local-cluster, so it reads fleet/hubs/<hubName>.yaml. hubName is set once at helm install, no default (Install PolicyStack).

# fleet/hubs/acm-dc1.yaml
revision: main
valueFiles:
  - environments/prod.yaml
  - datacenters/dc1.yaml
  - platforms/baremetal.yaml
  - acm/acm-dc1.yaml # (1)!
  1. Hubs in one datacenter share a layer by listing it.

hubName replaces the cluster name everywhere on the hub:

Managed cluster Hub Applications <element>-<cluster> <element>-<hubName> Cluster values file values/clusters/<cluster>.yaml values/clusters/<hubName>.yaml selectedName <cluster> <hubName>

Warning

Changing hubName renames the hub's Applications and every object they render.

Every hub reading the repo, DR hubs included, sets its own hubName. The chart fails without it rather than apply another hub's config. Check it with helm get values policystack -n openshift-gitops.

Why not use the cluster name?

Nothing on a hub is stable and unique. Every hub's ManagedCluster defaults to local-cluster. ACM's localClusterName (2.14+) changes only at install. clusterID changes on rebuild. hubs/ keeps hub files from colliding with a managed cluster of the same name.

A Global Hub managed hub imported in default mode has no local-cluster; the global hub reads its file instead (Global Hub).

items.title: Protection
items.text:
Other labels are ignored, and the five above are guarded by RBAC on ManagedClusters and openshift-gitops Secrets, so oc label cannot change what a cluster runs. Whoever merges to fleet/ decides, including destroying clusters with state: absent.

Add a CODEOWNERS entry and a default branch ruleset requiring code owner review and blocking force push and deletion:

# .github/CODEOWNERS
/fleet/ @<org>/<team>

To gate only production, own /fleet/prod-*.yaml and /fleet/hubs/ instead.

items.title: Generators
items.text:
policystack, rendered with hubName=acm-dc1:

generators:
  - matrix:
      generators:
        - matrix:
            generators:
              - clusters: # (1)!
                  selector:
                    matchExpressions:
                      - key: clusterID
                        operator: Exists
              - git: # (2)!
                  repoURL: 'https://github.com/PolicyStack/PolicyStack.git'
                  revision: HEAD
                  pathParamPrefix: fleet # (3)!
                  files:
                  - path: 'fleet/{{if index .metadata.labels "local-cluster"}}hubs/acm-dc1{{else if eq (index .metadata.labels "global-hub.open-cluster-management.io/deploy-mode") "default"}}hubs/{{.name}}{{else}}{{.name}}{{end}}.yaml'
        - git: # (4)!
            repoURL: 'https://github.com/PolicyStack/PolicyStack.git'
            revision: '{{.revision}}'
            directories:
            - path: 'stack/*'
  1. Every cluster secret with clusterID. The GitOpsCluster creates one per managed cluster.
  2. The cluster's fleet file at HEAD. Its keys become parameters. No file, no Applications.
  3. Stops the file's path from shadowing the element directory's path in the matrix.
  4. Every stack/* directory at the cluster's revision. One Application per cluster and directory.

An element added on a branch reaches only clusters pinned to a revision containing it. Disabled elements still get an Application that renders nothing.

items.title: Lifecycle generator
items.text:
policystack-lifecycle, rendered with hubName=acm-dc1:

generators:
  - matrix: # (1)!
      generators:
        - clusters:
            selector:
              matchExpressions:
                - key: local-cluster
                  operator: Exists
        - git: &fleet
            repoURL: 'https://github.com/PolicyStack/PolicyStack.git'
            revision: HEAD
            files:
            - path: 'fleet/*.yaml'
            - path: 'fleet/*/*.yaml' # (2)!
              exclude: true
          selector:
            matchExpressions:
              - key: hub
                operator: In
                values:
                  - "acm-dc1"
  - matrix: # (3)!
      generators:
        - git: *fleet
          selector:
            matchExpressions:
              - key: hub
                operator: Exists
        - clusters:
            selector:
              matchLabels:
                apps.open-cluster-management.io/cluster-name: '{{ if regexMatch "^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$" (toString .hub) }}{{ .hub }}{{ end }}' # (4)!
                global-hub.open-cluster-management.io/deploy-mode: default
  1. Fleet files with hub: acm-dc1, paired with this hub's own cluster secret. A hub that does not manage itself builds nothing.
  2. Argo CD's * crosses /. This drops hubs/ and other subdirectories.
  3. Fleet files naming a managed hub imported in default mode (Global Hub). Fleet files come first because Argo CD templates a child generator's fields but not its selector.
  4. A hub that is not a DNS label matches nothing instead of failing the whole ApplicationSet.

Files without hub match neither, so imported clusters get no lifecycle Application. The cluster secret's .name is the ManagedCluster the Policies are placed on.

items.title: Applications
items.text:
Field policystack policystack-lifecycle Name <element>-<cluster>, <element>-<hubName> on the hub lifecycle-<cluster> Source stack/<element> at the cluster's revision lifecycle/ at the fleet file's revision Values Cascade Same Destination Hub, open-cluster-management Same Sync Automated, prune, selfHeal, allowEmpty, RespectIgnoreDifferences=true Automated, prune, selfHeal

The Application name is the Helm release name, which every object name derives from (Naming limits). Argo CD deploys only to the hub; ACM delivers policies to clusters (Placement). Objects land in policyNamespace; the destination namespace is unused. allowEmpty lets a disabled element prune to zero objects (Disabling an element).

Both ApplicationSets set preserveResourcesOnDeletion: false: deleting an Application deletes its hub objects (Removing an element). Deleting a lifecycle Application leaves the cluster running unmanaged (Abandon).

Deletion is bounded

A failed render prunes nothing (ComparisonError). A failed generation deletes nothing. Argo CD only deletes hub objects; ACM then removes policies from the cluster (What happens on the managed cluster).

From policy-library 3.1.0, copyPolicyMetadata: false keeps Argo CD tracking metadata off ACM's per-cluster Policy copies, so Argo CD never prunes them. Clusters pinned to an older chart still copy it.

items.title: Render cache
items.text:
Each Application lists what its render reads in manifest-generate-paths. For compliance-prod-east-1:

argocd.argoproj.io/manifest-generate-paths: '.;../../values.yaml;../../values/environments/prod.yaml;../../values/datacenters/dc1.yaml;../../values/platforms/aws.yaml;../../values/clusters/prod-east-1.yaml'

A new commit re-renders only Applications whose listed paths changed. Fleet file changes alter the spec and always re-render. Without a webhook this needs Argo CD 2.11 (OpenShift GitOps 1.13)+; older versions re-render every Application on every commit.

items.title: Injected values
items.text:
Passed in valuesObject, which ranks above every values file (Order). For prod-east-1:

channel: "stable-4.20" # (1)!
selectedName: prod-east-1 # (2)!
selectedId: <clusterID>
selector:
  matchExpressions:
    name: # (3)!
      key: name
      operator: In
      values:
        - "prod-east-1"
  1. version and channel, only when the fleet file sets them.
  2. hubName on the hub.
  3. policy-library turns this into each Placement's selector. On the hub it holds the ManagedCluster name, not hubName.

Nothing else is injected. An element that needs the environment reads a key set in environments/<env>.yaml.

A lifecycle Application passes the fleet file's keys instead, so the fleet file's install overrides the cascade (Values):

hub: "acm-dc1"
state: "present"   # default
version: "4.20.8"  # channel too, when set
install: {}        # default
selector:
  matchExpressions:
    hub: # (1)!
      key: name
      operator: In
      values:
        - "local-cluster"
  1. The ManagedCluster of the hub running the lifecycle Policies.

items.title: The install chart
items.text:
The install chart installs both ApplicationSets, the GitOpsCluster and RBAC (Install PolicyStack).

Value Set in Use gitRepo --set Repo everything reads. Required. hubName --set This hub's identity (The hub). Required. policyNamespace install/values.yaml Must match the root values.yaml (CI checks). Do not change.

Upgrade it as in Upgrading. Preview the render:

helm template policystack ./install --set hubName=acm-dc1 --set gitRepo=https://github.com/PolicyStack/PolicyStack.git

items.title: Disconnected clusters
items.text:
Run oc-mirror v2 yourself. PolicyStack applies its output:

  • The disconnected element applies the mirror sets, catalogs and CA trust.
  • global.catalogSources points every operator at the mirrored catalog (Global keys).

Not covered

  • Image mirroring. oc-mirror's job.
  • The chart repo. Argo CD on the hub pulls policy-library from policystack.github.io, directly or through a proxy. Or mirror the chart and repoint every Chart.yaml.
  • Update Service. Run OSUS yourself; PolicyStack only points clusters at it (Update Service).

items.title: Site layer
items.text:
One datacenter layer holds the site data. List it in every fleet file at the site.

# values/datacenters/dc2.yaml
global:
  catalogSources:
    redhat-operators: cs-redhat-operator-index-v4-20 # (1)!

stack:
  disconnected:
    config:
      clusterResources: # (2)!
        - apiVersion: config.openshift.io/v1
          kind: ImageDigestMirrorSet
          metadata:
            name: idms-operator-0
          spec:
            imageDigestMirrors:
              - mirrors: [mirror.dc2.example.com:8443/redhat]
                source: registry.redhat.io/redhat
        - apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1
          kind: CatalogSource
          metadata:
            name: cs-redhat-operator-index-v4-20
            namespace: openshift-marketplace
          spec:
            image: mirror.dc2.example.com:8443/redhat/redhat-operator-index:v4.20
            sourceType: grpc
      registryCAs:
        mirror.dc2.example.com..8443: | # (3)!
          -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
          ...
      trustedCA: | # (4)!
        -----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----
        ...
  remediations:
    config:
      allowedRegistries: # (5)!
        - mirror.dc2.example.com:8443
        - quay.io
        - registry.redhat.io
        - image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000
  upgrade:
    config:
      upstream: https://osus.dc2.example.com/api/upgrades_info/v1/graph # (6)!
  1. A subscription.source the elements use, mapped to a CatalogSource in clusterResources.
  2. oc-mirror's working-dir/cluster-resources, unchanged.
  3. Registry host, with .. before a port.
  4. CAs of internal Git and Helm servers.
  5. Only with remediations enabled. Lists replace, so restate the defaults.
  6. Your OSUS graph. channel-pin writes it before the upgrade guard needs availableUpdates.

Enable it per cluster (Values cascade):

# values/clusters/prod-west-1.yaml
stack:
  disconnected:
    enabled: true

Release signatures

Each oc-mirror run adds release signature ConfigMaps to cluster-resources. Add them to clusterResources, or the cluster rejects that upgrade.

items.title: What the element applies
items.text:
All toggles default to true. Empty input renders nothing.

Toggle Applies resources config.clusterResources, as is. registry-ca ConfigMap openshift-config/registry-cas from config.registryCAs, and additionalTrustedCA on image.config.openshift.io/cluster. trusted-ca ConfigMap openshift-config/trusted-cas, with the Proxy's trustedCA pointing at it. Lands in every injected trust bundle, including the one the gitops element mounts into Argo CD's repo server. operatorhub OperatorHub disableAllDefaultSources: true.

items.title: trusted-cas
items.text:
Existing Proxy trustedCA

A Proxy pointing at a ConfigMap other than user-ca-bundle is repointed, and its CAs leave the trust bundle. Copy them into config.trustedCA first.

trusted-cas = user-ca-bundle (the installer's additionalTrustBundle) + config.trustedCA. user-ca-bundle is read on the cluster, never written.

Turning trusted-ca off

Turning the toggle off or emptying config.trustedCA leaves the Proxy on a stale trusted-cas, still trusted. Clean up by hand:

oc patch proxy/cluster --type merge -p '{"spec":{"trustedCA":{"name":"user-ca-bundle"}}}' # (1)!
oc delete configmap trusted-cas -n openshift-config
  1. Use "name":"" if user-ca-bundle does not exist.

items.title: Update Service
items.text:
The upgrade element holds a version until it shows in availableUpdates, so a disconnected cluster needs stack.upgrade.config.upstream (Site layer).

  • Put the OSUS CA in config.trustedCA, not registryCAs. The CVO trusts only trusted-ca-bundle, which the Proxy's trustedCA feeds.
  • Hub-built clusters run -multi payloads and the CVO asks for the multi graph. Mirror the multi release architecture, or availableUpdates stays empty.

items.title: Hosted clusters
items.text:
The HostedCluster owns mirrors, image config and proxy. Set them in the fleet file; the element keeps only the catalog.

Fleet fileCluster values 
# fleet/hcp-agent.yaml
install:
  hostedCluster:
    spec: # (1)!
      imageContentSources:
        - source: registry.redhat.io/redhat
          mirrors: [mirror.dc2.example.com:8443/redhat]
      additionalTrustBundle:
        name: mirror-ca # (2)!
      updateService: https://osus.dc2.example.com/api/upgrades_info/v1/graph # (3)!
  1. configuration (image, proxy) goes here too (Cluster lifecycle).
  2. Hub ConfigMap with key ca-bundle.crt in the HostedCluster's namespace. Create it with install.manifests (Install keys).
  3. The hosted CVO runs on the hub; use the OSUS Route URL. Without it, a version bump with channel set is held forever.
# values/clusters/hcp-agent.yaml
stack:
  disconnected:
    enabled: true
    toggles:
      registry-ca: false
      trusted-ca: false
    config:
      clusterResources: # (1)!
        - apiVersion: operators.coreos.com/v1alpha1
          kind: CatalogSource
          ...
  1. Replaces the site layer's list. CatalogSources only.

items.title: The hub
items.text:
The hub needs the mirrored catalogs before PolicyStack runs.

  1. Apply oc-mirror's output by hand:

    oc apply -f working-dir/cluster-resources/

  2. Install the operators with the site layer:

    helm template install/operators -f stack/acm/values.yaml -f stack/gitops/values.yaml \
  -f values/datacenters/dc2.yaml | oc apply -f -

  3. List datacenters/dc2.yaml in fleet/hubs/<hubName>.yaml and set stack.disconnected.enabled: true in values/clusters/<hubName>.yaml. The element takes over those objects.

items.title: Writing an element
items.text: An element is a Helm chart under stack/ that renders ACM policies through the policy-library chart. Every option of every policy type is in that README.

items.title: Naming
items.text:
• Lowercase kebab-case. Directory name and chart name must match: the Application and Helm release take the directory name (Applications), the values key takes the chart name, and element: dependencies and the validator assume both are equal.
  • Short: the common abbreviation (acm, odf) or a plain noun (logging). No openshift- prefix, no -operator suffix (Naming limits).
  • Must not start with another element's name plus -. gitops on cluster dev-c and gitops-dev on cluster c would both be release gitops-dev-c (POLICY091).
  • lifecycle is reserved.

Warning

Element and policy names are part of every object name. Renaming one recreates its Policies on every cluster.

items.title: Creating an element
items.text:
./tools/create-element.sh cert-manager "Certificate management"
# Created stack/cert-manager, values key stack.certManager. ...

It prompts for missing arguments, refuses a name that is not kebab-case or already exists, and copies tools/sample-element/ to stack/<name>/, replacing my-element with the name and myElement with its camelCase form. The result passes the validator as is. Then:

  1. Set the operator's namespace, operatorGroup and subscription in values.yaml.
  2. Replace converters/<name>-configmap.yaml with one file per templateNames entry. A missing converter fails (POLICY020), an unused one warns (POLICY021).
  3. Describe each toggle and setting with a comment above it and generate the README.
  4. Run the validator.
  5. Turn it on for one nonprod cluster in values/clusters/<cluster>.yaml.

items.title: Layout
items.text:
The files of tools/sample-element/. It has one of each piece: an operator under an install policy, a config policy that depends on it, a toggle, and one converter.

Chart.yamlvalues.yamlconverters/my-element-configmap.yamltemplates/policy.yaml.gitignore 
apiVersion: v2
name: my-element # (1)!
description: Example element. tools/create-element.sh copies it to stack/<name>.
type: application
version: 0.1.0
dependencies:
  - name: policy-library
    alias: stack # (2)!
    version: "3.4.0"
    repository: "https://policystack.github.io/PolicyStack-chart"
  1. Same as the directory name.
  2. The alias puts values under stack: and lets the library schema check them.
stack:
  myElement: # (1)!
    enabled: false # (2)!

    toggles:
      # Apply the ConfigMap configured below
      config: true # (3)!

    # Settings the converters read.
    config:
      # ConfigMap data, e.g. {logLevel: info}
      data: {} # (4)!

    default:
      categories:
        - CM Configuration Management
      controls:
        - CM-2 Baseline Configuration
      standards:
        - NIST SP 800-53

    policies:
      - name: install
        enabled: true
        description: "Install the operator"
        remediationAction: inform # (5)!
        severity: medium
        disabled: false

      - name: config
        enabled: true
        description: "Configure the operator"
        remediationAction: inform
        severity: medium
        disabled: false
        # ACM holds this policy Pending until install is compliant
        dependencies:
          - name: install

    operatorPolicies:
      my-element:
        enabled: true
        description: "Example operator"
        displayName: "Example Operator"
        policyRef: install # (6)!
        severity: medium
        remediationAction: inform
        complianceType: musthave
        namespace: my-element
        operatorGroup:
          name: my-element
        subscription:
          channel: stable
          name: my-element-operator
          source: redhat-operators
          sourceNamespace: openshift-marketplace
        upgradeApproval: Automatic
        # Allowed CSV names; empty allows whatever the channel offers
        versions: [] # (7)!

    configPolicies:
      - name: my-element-config # (8)!
        enabled: true
        description: "Example ConfigMap"
        policyRef: config
        complianceType: musthave
        remediationAction: inform
        severity: medium
        # Wait for the operator's CSV, and stay compliant while waiting
        waitForOperator: my-element
        ignorePending: true
        templateNames:
          - name: my-element-configmap # (9)!
  1. camelCase of the chart name (Element values).
  2. Off by default. A layer in values/ turns it on.
  3. Overrides enabled of the entry named config.
  4. Site data. Converters read it, layers set it.
  5. New policies start in inform.
  6. The policy this operator renders into.
  7. Pin versions in layers, not here (Operator upgrades).
  8. Prefixed with the element name: template names must be unique across all Policies on a cluster.
  9. Renders converters/my-element-configmap.yaml.
{{- /* One object per converter. Site data comes from config, not hard-coded values. */ -}}
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: my-element
  namespace: my-element
data:
  {{- toYaml .Values.stack.myElement.config.data | nindent 2 }}

{{- include "policy-library.render" . -}}

Chart.lock
*.tgz
charts/

A converter is the manifest for one configPolicies[].templateNames entry, rendered with Helm's tpl. It reads .Values, and .Parameters (that config policy's templateParameters) when the config policy sets enableTemplateParameters: true. README.md is generated.

items.title: Conventions
items.text:
From stack/metallb:

Convention metallb Off by default enabled: false; a values layer turns it on Toggles for optional pieces toggles.quota and toggles.addressing ship false; a cluster flips one in one line instead of restating the policies list A config map for site data Converters read config.ipAddressPools, l2Advertisements, bgpPeers, quota. Maps merge (Merge rules), so a cluster sets only its keys Install, then configure config depends on install, addressing on config. ACM holds each Pending until the previous one is compliant (dependencies) Wait for the CSV metallb-instance sets waitForOperator: metallb and ignorePending: true, so it waits for the operator without going noncompliant (waiting for an operator) rawTemplate when the object count varies Pool, advertisement and peer converters emit one object per map key. An empty map renders an empty list (raw object templates) Short names Element, policy, config and operator policy names end up in length-limited object names (Naming limits)

A cluster turning it on, values/clusters/nonprod-west-1.yaml:

stack:
  metallb:
    enabled: true
    toggles:
      addressing: true
    config:
      ipAddressPools:
        services: # (1)!
          addresses:
            - 10.20.30.100-10.20.30.120
          autoAssign: true
      l2Advertisements:
        services:
          ipAddressPools:
            - services
  1. Map key is the object name, value is the IPAddressPool spec.

The rawTemplate converter that reads it, converters/metallb-ipaddresspools.yaml:

{{- range $name, $spec := .Values.stack.metallb.config.ipAddressPools }}
- complianceType: mustonlyhave
  objectDefinition:
    apiVersion: metallb.io/v1beta1
    kind: IPAddressPool
    metadata:
      name: {{ $name }}
      namespace: {{ $.Parameters.namespace }} # (1)!
    spec:{{ toYaml $spec | nindent 6 }}
{{- end }}
  1. From the pools config policy's templateParameters.

items.title: Good practices
items.text:
• One product per element. Clusters turn an element on as a unit. An operator and its configuration belong together, unrelated settings do not.
  • Prefix config and operator policy names with the element. Two elements that both put a ns-monitoring config policy under an install policy render the same template name install-ns-monitoring and collide on the cluster (POLICY003). metallb uses metallb-instance.
  • Start in inform. Roll out to a nonprod revision, read compliance, then switch to enforce.
  • Pin operator versions in layers. Ship versions: [], set it per environment or cluster (Operator upgrades).
  • Try changes on one cluster first. Push a branch, then pin a nonprod cluster's fleet file to it with a pull request to the default branch (Promoting and rolling back).

Policy-level remediationAction overrides inform gates

ACM applies it to every template in the Policy but InformOnly ones, so enforce there enforces readiness checks and mustnothave signals. Set gates to InformOnly (config policies only), as lifecycle, upgrade and storage-nodes do, or leave the Policy's action unset and set it on each config and operator policy, as acs and cert-manager do. global.remediationAction: inform still overrides all of them.

pruneObjectBehavior decides whether removal deletes objects

Set it only on templates without dependencies (POLICY033), in its own commit, so it reaches the cluster before the removal (What happens on the managed cluster).

Keep the branch until the pin moves back

A fleet file pinned to a deleted branch freezes the Applications of every cluster (Revision).

items.title: Secrets
items.text:
Values live in Git. Read runtime secrets on the hub with an ACM hub template, escaped so Helm passes it through. From stack/acs/converters/acs-sync-crs.yaml:

data: '{{ "{{" }}hub copySecretData "{{ .Parameters.hubNamespace }}" "cluster-registration-secret" hub{{ "}}" }}'

copySecretData copies every key of data, not the type, labels or annotations. fromSecret reads one key and returns '' when it is missing.

Hub lookups are limited to the policy namespace. To read another, point the policy at a ServiceAccount in the policy namespace that can read it, as acs does:

policies:
  - name: secured # (1)!
    hubTemplateOptions:
      serviceAccountName: acs-hub-templates
  1. Trimmed; see stack/acs/values.yaml.

The validator evaluates escaped templates as POLICY081 (ACM templates).

items.title: Element reference
items.text:
stack/<element>/README.md is generated from Chart.yaml and values.yaml. Do not edit it by hand.

pip install -r tools/requirements.txt
python tools/doc-generator.py          # regenerate all READMEs
python tools/doc-generator.py --check  # report stale ones, write nothing

It shows the values key, toggles, settings (config), operators, and each Policy with its templates as they appear in the ACM console. Descriptions come from:

Source Shown as Chart.yaml description Lead paragraph Chart.yaml home Guide link, for elements with a page under docs/ Comment above toggles: or config: Section intro Comment above a key under toggles or config That row's description description: of a policy, config or operator policy Policy line or template row 
config:
  # Ceph CSI tolerations are not managed: see the converter. # (1)!

  # Device sets per replica
  count: 2
  1. A blank line separates a maintainer note from the key. Comments anywhere else are never rendered.

A map under config is listed key by key when its values are all scalars or any of its keys has a comment; otherwise it is one row, with long defaults folded below the table.

Commit the README with the values.yaml change. CI runs the check on pull requests, and the update-docs label regenerates READMEs on the PR branch (Documentation Check).

items.title: Global Hub
items.text: Running PolicyStack when ACM hubs sit under a Multicluster Global Hub.

items.title: What Global Hub does
items.text:
Global Hub is an operator on one ACM hub, the global hub. The ACM hubs it imports are managed hubs. An agent on each managed hub streams its Policies, compliance, events and ManagedClusters through Kafka into PostgreSQL, and Grafana reads them there. It can also move clusters between managed hubs (ManagedClusterMigration, Technology Preview).

It does not push configuration. Global policy distribution was removed in 1.7. PolicyStack and each hub's ACM still deliver everything.

Minimum version

Use Global Hub 1.8.2 (RHSA-2026:68515) or 1.7.3 (RHSA-2026:67842) or later. Earlier releases let one managed hub spoof another's compliance data (CVE-2026-71576). 1.8 pairs with ACM 2.17, 1.7 with 2.16.

items.title: Import modes
items.text:
A label on the managed hub's ManagedCluster (on the global hub) picks the mode. No label, no Global Hub agent.

apiVersion: cluster.open-cluster-management.io/v1
kind: ManagedCluster
metadata:
  name: hub-a # (1)!
  labels:
    global-hub.open-cluster-management.io/deploy-mode: default # (2)!
  1. Must match the managed hub's hubName. Default mode finds the hub's files by this name, hosted mode by hubName, so matching them means a mode change moves no file. Global Hub also shows this name in its dashboards.
  2. default or hosted.
default hosted Managed hub's klusterlet runs on The managed hub The global hub Managed hub has local-cluster No (disableHubSelfManagement: true) Yes Global hub's Policies reach the managed hub Yes No. The webhook disables the policy and application addons Reads fleet/hubs/<managed-hub>.yaml Global hub Managed hub Builds the managed hub's clusters Global hub, placed on the managed hub (Lifecycle) Managed hub hypershift engine on the managed hub No Yes When to set the label Any time Before import. Already-imported clusters are ignored Hosted mode requirements
  • The global hub manages itself.
  • The import kubeconfig never expires.
  • The global hub reaches each managed hub's API.
  • Backup and restore of the managed hub is not supported.

items.title: Layout
items.text:
Install PolicyStack on the global hub and on every managed hub, each with its own hubName (Install PolicyStack). All hubs read the same fleet/. A hub's ApplicationSets only see the ManagedClusters it imports, so each fleet file renders Day-2 on one hub and lifecycle on one hub. For a cluster under a default-mode hub those differ: Day-2 renders on the managed hub, lifecycle on the global hub.

fleet/
  hubs/gh.yaml      # the global hub
  hubs/hub-a.yaml   # default-mode managed hub, read by gh
  hubs/hub-b.yaml   # hosted-mode managed hub, read by hub-b
  edge-1.yaml       # hub: hub-a, built by gh on hub-a
  edge-2.yaml       # hub: hub-b, built by hub-b
Default modeHosted mode

Turn off local-cluster in the managed hub's values. Left at true, the acm element turns it back on and breaks the import.

# values/acm/hub-a.yaml, listed in fleet/hubs/hub-a.yaml
stack:
  acm:
    config:
      selfManaged: false

Then:

  1. Commit fleet/hubs/hub-a.yaml.

  2. Label the ManagedCluster.

    oc label managedcluster hub-a global-hub.open-cluster-management.io/deploy-mode=default

The label picks the fleet file

With the label, the global hub reads fleet/hubs/hub-a.yaml. Without it, fleet/hub-a.yaml. Removing the label deletes the hub's Day-2 Policies (Removing an element).

  • Do not name a managed cluster after the hub that manages it. The global hub's Policies for hub-a land in namespace hub-a on hub-a, where a managed cluster hub-a would collide.
  • A hub the global hub builds also has fleet/hub-a.yaml for its lifecycle keys. After import, its upgrade version and channel go in fleet/hubs/hub-a.yaml.

Set the label in the ManagedCluster before importing. Nothing else changes on the managed hub: it keeps local-cluster and reads its own fleet/hubs/hub-b.yaml.

Warning

Do not create fleet/hub-b.yaml for Day-2. The global hub would render Policies that never reach the hub.

items.title: Lifecycle
items.text:
policystack-lifecycle has two generators (Lifecycle generator):

Generator Matches fleet files whose hub is Places the Policy on 1 This hub's hubName, if this hub has local-cluster local-cluster 2 A ManagedCluster of this hub labeled deploy-mode=default That managed hub

The global hub and hosted-mode hubs build their own clusters with generator 1. A default-mode hub has no local-cluster, so it renders nothing and the global hub builds for it with generator 2.

# fleet/edge-1.yaml, rendered by gh, Policy placed on hub-a
revision: main
hub: hub-a
version: 4.20.8
channel: stable-4.20
install:
  engine: hive
  credential:
    namespace: hive-credentials
    name: aws                     # (1)!
  baseDomain: aws.example.com
  hive:
    platform:
      aws:
        region: us-east-2
  1. The Secret must exist on hub-a, not the global hub.

ACM delivers the Policies to the managed hub, where every lookup and fromSecret resolves. The credential and BMC Secrets live on the managed hub in both modes.

No hypershift on a default-mode hub

The HyperShift operator is not installed there, so present-lifecycle-<cluster> stays NonCompliant. Use hive, siteconfig, or hosted mode.

Changing a managed hub's mode
  1. Detach the hub from the global hub.
  2. Flip stack.acm.config.selfManaged.
  3. Re-import with the new label.

Fleet files stay where they are. hive and siteconfig clusters survive and the other hub adopts them: no lifecycle Policy sets pruneObjectBehavior and hub is unchanged (Abandon). hypershift clusters cannot change mode.

items.title: Do not
items.text:
• Label a PolicyStack hub global-hub.open-cluster-management.io/hub-role. Hub HA copies its ApplicationSets, Applications, Policies and ArgoCD CR to the standby.
  • Enable the ACM gitops-addon or Argo CD Agent on a managed hub. They replace openshift-gitops, which runs that hub's PolicyStack.
  • Reuse a cluster name across hubs. fleet/ is shared and migration needs unique names.
  • Migrate a lifecycle-built cluster with ManagedClusterMigration. It moves the ManagedCluster, not its Policies or Applications, and hypershift clusters cannot migrate. Imported clusters migrate cleanly: the target hub picks up the same fleet/<cluster>.yaml. Then re-register them with ACS (steps 2-3).

items.title: Installation
items.text:
PolicyStack runs on the ACM hub. You install it once per hub with Helm, from install/. After that, everything is driven from Git. Run every command from the root of your fork, logged in to the hub as a cluster administrator.

  1. Check the prerequisites
  2. Install the operators (new hubs only)
  3. Install PolicyStack
  4. Add the hub's fleet file
  5. Hand the operators to PolicyStack (later, once the stack is proven)
Placeholder Meaning Example <hub> The hub's name in PolicyStack (hubName). Picks fleet/hubs/<hub>.yaml. Unique per active hub reading the repo. A DR hub takes over the hubName of the hub it replaces (Hub disaster recovery). acm-dc1 <org>/<fork> Your GitHub org and fork of PolicyStack acme/policystack

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
• oc, and helm 3.14 or later (3.18 or later for --take-ownership).
  • A fork of PolicyStack, cloned locally. Argo CD reads your fleet files and values from it; upstream ships none.
  • A hub that already runs OpenShift GitOps must use its default Argo CD instance, openshift-gitops.
  • A hub that builds clusters from fleet files needs ACM 2.16 or later (Cluster lifecycle prerequisites).
git clone https://github.com/<org>/<fork>.git && cd <fork>
helm version --short                # v3.14.0 or later
oc auth can-i '*' '*' --all-namespaces   # yes
Private fork: add a repository secret

Argo CD needs credentials to read a private repo (Argo CD docs):

apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: policystack-repo
  namespace: openshift-gitops
  labels:
    argocd.argoproj.io/secret-type: repository
stringData:
  type: git
  url: https://github.com/<org>/<fork>.git
  username: <user>
  password: <token>  # (1)!
  1. A personal access token with read access to the fork.

Apply it after openshift-gitops exists, before Install PolicyStack.

items.title: Install the operators
items.text:
New hubHub that already runs ACM/GitOps

Installs ACM and OpenShift GitOps and creates the MultiClusterHub. The loop retries every 30 seconds while the operators install their CRDs. If it never ends, stop it and read the oc error, usually an unreachable catalog.

until helm template install/operators -f stack/acm/values.yaml -f stack/gitops/values.yaml \
      | oc apply -f - && oc get argocd/openshift-gitops -n openshift-gitops; do sleep 30; done

Verify. The MultiClusterHub takes about 10 minutes:

oc wait mch/multiclusterhub -n open-cluster-management --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Running --timeout=20m
# multiclusterhub.operator.open-cluster-management.io/multiclusterhub condition met
oc wait argocd/openshift-gitops -n openshift-gitops --for=jsonpath='{.status.phase}'=Available --timeout=10m
# argocd.argoproj.io/openshift-gitops condition met

These are the same objects the acm and gitops elements enforce, so handover adopts them in place. The chart installs the channel head and refuses versions or upgradeApproval pins; pin after handover (Operator upgrades).

Single node or disconnected hub

Add a values layer to helm template with -f:

# values/acm/<hub>.yaml
stack:
  acm:
    config:
      availabilityConfig: Basic  # (1)!
  1. Single replicas, for lab and single node hubs. The default is High.
until helm template install/operators -f stack/acm/values.yaml -f stack/gitops/values.yaml \
      -f values/acm/<hub>.yaml | oc apply -f - && oc get argocd/openshift-gitops -n openshift-gitops; do sleep 30; done

On a disconnected hub, also add the layer that sets global.catalogSources, such as -f values/datacenters/<dc>.yaml (Disconnected clusters).

Skip this step. Your operators keep running as they are. Run the compatibility checks under Hand the operators to PolicyStack before enabling the acm or gitops element.

items.title: Install PolicyStack
items.text:
Creates the ApplicationSets, the pstack policy namespace, the cluster import into Argo CD and its RBAC.

helm install policystack ./install -n openshift-gitops \
  --set hubName=<hub> --set gitRepo=https://github.com/<org>/<fork>.git \
  --description "$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"

Both values are required and stored in the release; upgrades reuse them. --description records the commit, which upgrades compare against.

Verify:

oc get applicationsets -n openshift-gitops
# NAME                    AGE
# policystack             10s
# policystack-lifecycle   10s
oc get secrets -n openshift-gitops -l argocd.argoproj.io/secret-type=cluster
# one secret per ManagedCluster, including the hub
Object Name Namespace Purpose ApplicationSet policystack openshift-gitops One Application per element per cluster (Applications) ApplicationSet policystack-lifecycle openshift-gitops One Application per cluster this hub builds (Lifecycle generator) Namespace pstack Holds the Policies ManagedClusterSetBinding global openshift-gitops, pstack Lets Placements select every cluster Placement global openshift-gitops Every cluster, tolerating unreachable and unavailable GitOpsCluster argo-acm-importer-global openshift-gitops Creates an Argo CD cluster secret per selected cluster ClusterRole, ClusterRoleBinding openshift-gitops-policy-admin Lets the Argo CD application controller manage Policies, PolicySets, Placements and PlacementBindings, the only objects elements render

Not in ACM backup

The ApplicationSets, their Applications, the Placement and the GitOpsCluster carry velero.io/exclude-from-backup: "true". A restored policystack-lifecycle on a passive hub would build the old hub's clusters there.

Objects outlive the release

Every object carries helm.sh/resource-policy: keep. helm uninstall policystack leaves PolicyStack running. To remove it, see Teardown.

If Helm reports an object that already exists, such as a hand-made global binding, rerun with --take-ownership (Helm 3.18 or later) to adopt it.

items.title: Add the hub's fleet file
items.text:
The hub gets Applications only once its fleet file is on the default branch (The hub):

# fleet/hubs/<hub>.yaml
revision: main  # (1)!
valueFiles:  # (2)!
  - environments/prod.yaml
  - datacenters/dc1.yaml
  - acm/<hub>.yaml
  1. Branch, tag or SHA the hub's Applications render from (Revision).
  2. Layers under values/, lowest precedence first (Order). values/clusters/<hub>.yaml is always added last.

Merge it to the default branch. Within about 6 minutes, each element under stack/ gets an Application named <element>-<hub>:

oc get applications.argoproj.io -n openshift-gitops | grep <hub>
# acm-<hub>      Synced   Healthy
# gitops-<hub>   Synced   Healthy
# ...

An element no layer enables syncs with no resources. Managed clusters follow the same pattern with fleet/<cluster>.yaml (Onboarding a cluster).

items.title: Hand the operators to PolicyStack
items.text:
Once the rest of the stack is proven on the hub, let the acm and gitops elements own the operators.

Existing hub: check compatibility first

An element adopts an operator only when the namespace, OperatorGroup name and Subscription name (which must equal the package) match the element.

oc get subscriptions.operators.coreos.com -A \
  -o custom-columns=NS:.metadata.namespace,NAME:.metadata.name,PACKAGE:.spec.name,CHANNEL:.spec.channel \
  | grep -E 'advanced-cluster-management|openshift-gitops-operator'
oc get operatorgroups -n <NS>   # <NS> from the first command
Element Namespace OperatorGroup Subscription acm open-cluster-management open-cluster-management advanced-cluster-management gitops openshift-gitops-operator openshift-gitops-operator openshift-gitops-operator Mismatch Fix NAME differs from PACKAGE Leave that element off. The OperatorPolicy would create a second Subscription. NS differs, such as GitOps in openshift-operators Set namespace and operatorGroup.name to match, or leave the element off. Otherwise OLM installs the operator twice. Console-created OperatorGroup, <ns>-xxxxx Set operatorGroup.name to it. Older channel Set subscription.channel to it, then move one minor at a time.

Overrides go in values/acm/<hub>.yaml:

stack:
  gitops:
    operatorPolicies:
      gitops:
        namespace: openshift-operators
        operatorGroup:
          name: global-operators

# values/acm/<hub>.yaml, listed in fleet/hubs/<hub>.yaml valueFiles
stack:
  acm:
    enabled: true
  gitops:
    enabled: true
    toggles:
      instance: false  # (1)!
      link: false  # (2)!
  1. PolicyStack never reconciles the Argo CD instance that delivers it. A bad value there would break the path that fixes it.
  2. The console link depends on instance.

Warning

Do not run Install the operators after handover. It resets any channel the hub layer overrides.

ACM and GitOps upgrades now follow the hub's fleet revision like any other element (Operator upgrades).

items.title: Upgrading
items.text:
Part How Elements, lifecycle, values Merge upstream into the fork, then move fleet revision pins (Rolling out changes) ACM and GitOps Through the elements after handover. Before it, OLM upgrades within the installed channel. The install chart helm upgrade, below Upgrade the install chart

The ApplicationSets are not pinned per cluster: a change under install/templates/ reaches every cluster on the hub at once. Upgrade only when the git diff below prints changes:

helm history policystack -n openshift-gitops   # DESCRIPTION of the deployed revision = <last>
git diff <last>..HEAD -- install/

If the deployed revision's DESCRIPTION reads Rollback to <n>, use revision <n>'s DESCRIPTION as <last>.

helm upgrade policystack ./install -n openshift-gitops --reset-then-reuse-values \
  --description "$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"

--reset-then-reuse-values takes the new chart defaults and keeps hubName and gitRepo. Roll back with helm rollback policystack <revision> -n openshift-gitops.

From the appset chart

Hubs installed with the old appset release and gitops-prereq/ move over once, with Helm 3.18 or later. <ns> is the namespace of the appset release.

  1. Check the stored manifest keeps all four objects. The ApplicationSets gained keep on 2026-10-13. Below 4, run helm upgrade appset once, with its usual values, from a commit before install/ existed.

    helm get manifest appset -n <ns> | grep -c 'helm.sh/resource-policy'   # 4

  2. Move the release. Reusing the stored values keeps hubName exact; a different one renames and recreates every hub Application.

    helm get values appset -n <ns> -o yaml > appset-values.yaml
helm uninstall appset -n <ns>
helm install policystack ./install -n openshift-gitops --take-ownership -f appset-values.yaml \
  --description "$(git rev-parse --short HEAD)"
oc get applicationset policystack -n openshift-gitops \
  -o jsonpath='{.metadata.annotations.meta\.helm\.sh/release-name}'   # policystack

    Nothing is deleted. If the old ApplicationSet had preserveResourcesOnDeletion: true, its Applications gain the resources finalizer, and an Application left OutOfSync on a disabled element prunes on its next automated sync.

  3. Drop the cluster-admin binding the old install created. Skip this if the openshift-gitops instance also syncs Applications outside PolicyStack; they may rely on it.

    oc auth can-i create policies.policy.open-cluster-management.io -n pstack \
  --as=system:serviceaccount:openshift-gitops:openshift-gitops-argocd-application-controller   # yes
oc get clusterrolebinding -o wide | grep 'ClusterRole/cluster-admin' | grep openshift-gitops-argocd-application-controller
oc adm policy remove-cluster-role-from-user cluster-admin -z openshift-gitops-argocd-application-controller \
  -n openshift-gitops --rolebinding-name=<name>   # <name> from the previous command

    Danger

    Without --rolebinding-name, the last command edits every cluster-admin binding. Never delete openshift-gitops-policy-admin: nothing recreates it before the next helm upgrade.

  4. Sync the Applications and check they stay Synced.

items.title: Teardown
items.text:
oc delete applicationset policystack policystack-lifecycle -n openshift-gitops

Deletes every Policy

This deletes every Application and every Policy they rendered (Removing an element). Clusters this hub built keep running, unmanaged (Abandon). Add --cascade=orphan to keep the Applications and Policies.

items.title: Lifecycle reference
items.text: Details behind Cluster lifecycle. Chart: lifecycle/.

items.title: Install keys
items.text:
Defaults are in lifecycle/values.yaml. The schema rejects unknown keys, and rejects hive or siteconfig keys unless engine selects them.

Key Default Notes engine hypershift hypershift, hive or siteconfig. Fixed at create. credential.namespace, .name required Hub Secret with pullSecret, ssh-publickey, and for hive the cloud keys (vSphere: username, password, cacertificate). Any namespace. baseDomain "" Required except on KubeVirt, which uses the hub's ingress domain. Fixed at create. releaseRepository quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release Image is <releaseRepository>:<version>-multi. Point at a mirror when disconnected. manifests [] Extra hub objects with apiVersion, kind, metadata. Created before the cluster, deleted after it. hypershifthivesiteconfig Key Default Notes platform required KubeVirt, Agent or None. Fixed at create. namespace clusters HostedCluster, NodePools and copied secrets. Control plane runs in <namespace>-<cluster>. agentNamespace "" InfraEnv and Agents. Required on Agent. services APIServer: LoadBalancer, others Route Service to servicePublishingStrategy. HyperShift needs all four. Fixed at create. hostedCluster {} metadata and spec merged over the generated HostedCluster. spec.release is ignored. nodePools {} Pool to NodePool spec, merged over the generated one. Named <cluster>-<pool>.

hcp-agent after the cascade merges platforms/agent.yaml, values/clusters/hcp-agent.yaml and its fleet file, trimmed:

install:
  platform: Agent                    # (1)!
  agentNamespace: hardware-inventory
  credential:
    namespace: hcp-credentials
    name: hostinventory
  services:
    APIServer:
      type: LoadBalancer
      loadBalancer:
        hostname: api-int-hcp-agent.dc1.example.com
    OAuthServer:
      type: Route                    # (2)!
    Konnectivity:
      type: Route
    Ignition:
      type: Route
  hostedCluster:
    spec:
      kubeAPIServerDNSName: api-hcp-agent.dc1.example.com
  nodePools:
    compute:                         # (3)!
      replicas: 3
      platform:
        agent:
          agentLabelSelector:
            matchLabels:
              example.com/class: fc830
  manifests:
    - apiVersion: metallb.io/v1beta1 # (4)!
      kind: IPAddressPool
      metadata:
        name: hcp-agent-apiserver
        namespace: metallb-system
      spec:
        addresses:
          - 10.20.9.13/32
  1. From platforms/agent.yaml. Every layer of the values cascade can set install.
  2. Maps merge with the defaults, so setting only APIServer keeps the other three. null drops an entry.
  3. NodePool hcp-agent-compute. A pool without agentLabelSelector claims any free Agent in agentNamespace.
  4. Exists before the HostedCluster, so MetalLB has the address when the kube-apiserver Service asks for one.
Key Default Notes hive.platform required Exactly one of aws, gcp, azure, vsphere. Needs region; GCP adds projectID, Azure baseDomainResourceGroupName. vSphere is the installer's platform.vsphere: needs vcenters and failureDomains, refuses user/password. Fixed at create. hive.installConfig {} Merged under the generated install-config. Hive drops fields its installer does not know. hive.clusterDeployment {} metadata and spec merged over the generated ClusterDeployment. spec.provisioning.releaseImage is ignored. 
# values/platforms/aws.yaml, trimmed
install:
  engine: hive
  credential:
    namespace: hive-credentials
    name: aws                       # (1)!
  hive:
    installConfig:
      controlPlane:
        name: master
        replicas: 3
        platform:
          aws:
            type: m6i.xlarge
      networking:
        networkType: OVNKubernetes

# fleet/hive-aws.yaml
install:
  baseDomain: aws.example.com
  hive:
    platform:
      aws:
        region: us-east-2           # (2)!
  1. Holds pullSecret, ssh-publickey, aws_access_key_id, aws_secret_access_key.
  2. Goes to both the install-config and the ClusterDeployment.
Key Default Notes siteconfig.templates ai ai (assisted installer) or ibi (image-based, single node). Fixed at create. siteconfig.templateNamespace open-cluster-management Namespace of the stock <templates>-cluster-templates-v1 and <templates>-node-templates-v1 ConfigMaps. siteconfig.bmcCredential.namespace, .name required Hub Secret with username and password, copied to <cluster>-bmc. siteconfig.clusterInstance {} Merged under the generated ClusterInstance spec. siteconfig.nodes required hostName to ClusterInstance node. bmcAddress and bootMACAddress required. Layers merge per host. 
# values/platforms/baremetal.yaml
install:
  engine: siteconfig
  credential:
    namespace: bm-credentials
    name: hostinventory
  siteconfig:
    bmcCredential:
      namespace: bm-credentials
      name: bmc
    clusterInstance:
      networkType: OVNKubernetes

# fleet/sno-edge.yaml
install:
  siteconfig:
    clusterInstance:
      clusterType: SNO
      machineNetwork:
        - cidr: 10.20.30.0/24
    nodes:
      sno-edge.dc1.example.com:     # (1)!
        role: master
        bmcAddress: redfish-virtualmedia://10.20.0.11/redfish/v1/Systems/1
        bootMACAddress: "00:11:22:33:44:55"
  1. The key becomes hostName. ibi allows one node; ai with -multi at most 3 control-plane nodes.

items.title: Generated objects
items.text:
<cluster> is the fleet file name. Everything not listed uses the operator's defaults: set it in hostedCluster, hive.clusterDeployment or siteconfig.clusterInstance.

hypershifthivesiteconfig Object Content HostedCluster <namespace>/<cluster> Release image, pullSecret <cluster>-pull-secret, sshKey <cluster>-ssh-key, platform, services, channel and dns.baseDomain when set. Agent adds agentNamespace. Agent and None add secretEncryption with <cluster>-etcd-encryption-key. NodePool <namespace>/<cluster>-<pool> clusterName, release image, platform, management.upgradeType (Replace on KubeVirt, else InPlace). No replicas means 0.

etcd encryption key

Generated once, while neither the key nor the HostedCluster exists. A deleted key is never regenerated: a new key cannot decrypt etcd. Restore it from backup.

Object Content ClusterDeployment <cluster>/<cluster> baseDomain, clusterName, platform with credentialsSecretRef <cluster>-creds, pullSecretRef, installConfigSecretRef <cluster>-install-config, release image, installAttemptsLimit: 1 (a failed install is not retried). vSphere: infrastructure is hive.platform.vsphere with a blank login, plus certificatesSecretRef <cluster>-certs. Secret <cluster>-creds Only the keys Hive reads: aws_access_key_id + aws_secret_access_key, osServiceAccount.json, osServicePrincipal.json, or username + password. Secret <cluster>-certs vSphere: .cacert from cacertificate. The login goes only into <cluster>-install-config. ManagedCluster <cluster>, KlusterletAddonConfig Every add-on on. Object Content ClusterImageSet lifecycle-<cluster> The release image. ClusterInstance <cluster>/<cluster> clusterName, baseDomain, pullSecretRef, sshPublicKey, templates, clusterImageSetNameRef, per node hostName, bmcCredentialsName <cluster>-bmc and node templates. SiteConfig defaults bootMode: UEFI, automatedCleaningMode: disabled. KlusterletAddonConfig Every add-on on. The stock ai one turns application-manager off, so ACM would never create the Argo CD secret. The chart suppresses it and renders its own.

Hive and SiteConfig reject release image changes, and SiteConfig any spec change before install completes. The chart reads those fields back from the live objects, so a version bump or credential rotation never touches them. Those clusters upgrade through upgrade.

items.title: Policy chains
items.text:
The hub gets present-lifecycle-<cluster> or absent-lifecycle-<cluster>, picked by state. Each template waits for the one before it to be Compliant.

flowchart LR
  subgraph present
    pg[guard] --> pc[credentials] --> pm[manifests] --> pcl[cluster] --> pr[ready]
  end
  subgraph absent
    ag[guard] --> ad[detach] --> adt[detached] --> ax[destroy] --> axd[destroyed] --> acl[cleanup]
  end

Templates are named <state>-<step>-<cluster>, e.g. present-guard-hcp-kubevirt. siteconfig has no detach or detached.

present-lifecycle-<cluster>:

Template Mode hypershift hive siteconfig guard InformOnly NonCompliant while something named <cluster> lacks the marker. Stops the chain. same same credentials enforce Namespace install.namespace, <cluster>-pull-secret, <cluster>-ssh-key, etcd key on Agent/None Namespace <cluster>, -pull-secret, -creds, -install-config, -certs on vSphere Namespace <cluster>, -pull-secret, -bmc manifests enforce install.manifests same same cluster enforce HostedCluster, NodePools ClusterDeployment, ManagedCluster, KlusterletAddonConfig ClusterImageSet, ClusterInstance, KlusterletAddonConfig ready InformOnly version is the desired and newest Completed version, and on every NodePool spec.installed: true Provisioned True

absent-lifecycle-<cluster>:

Template Mode hypershift hive siteconfig guard InformOnly Same check same same detach enforce mustnothave Deletes the ManagedCluster while the cluster is up, so the klusterlet cleans up same none: SiteConfig would re-create it detached InformOnly mustnothave Waits for the ManagedCluster to go same none destroy enforce mustnothave Deletes the HostedCluster Deletes the ClusterDeployment; Hive deprovisions with <cluster>-creds (and -certs on vSphere) Deletes the ClusterInstance and what it rendered destroyed InformOnly mustnothave Waits for the HostedCluster to go Waits for deprovision Waits for the ClusterInstance to go cleanup enforce Copied secrets, etcd key, install.manifests Namespace <cluster>, install.manifests Namespace <cluster>, ClusterImageSet, install.manifests
  • An enforced delete is Compliant once the API accepts it, so every destroy step has an inform wait after it.
  • Create templates are musthave: operator-filled fields are not compared, so the Policy never fights HyperShift, Hive or SiteConfig.
  • The credential is never deleted.
  • Every enforced step but manifests repeats the ownership check in the same evaluation and fails on a foreign object, so a stale guard result never lets it write or delete.

Note

No lifecycle template sets pruneObjectBehavior. Deleting the present Policy deletes nothing; only state: absent destroys.

items.title: Day-2 handoff
items.text:
1. The ManagedCluster appears. hypershift: the hypershift-addon creates it once the HostedCluster is available. hive, siteconfig: ACM imports the one the chart or SiteConfig created.
  2. It joins global, the GitOpsCluster creates its Argo CD secret, and ACM adds the clusterID label (Install PolicyStack).
  3. The Day-2 ApplicationSet pairs the secret with the same fleet file and creates <element>-<cluster> Applications. It ignores hub, state and install.

Labels in hostedCluster.metadata.labels are copied to the ManagedCluster once, at creation.

HyperShift auto-import disabled

Auto-import is on by default. autoImportDisabled in the hypershift-addon-deploy-config AddOnDeploymentConfig leaves a built cluster without Day-2 until you import it by hand.

items.title: Ownership
items.text:
Lifecycle acts only on what it built: objects carrying the annotation lifecycle.policystk.io/hub: <hubName>, written by present-cluster-<cluster> in the create itself. Only the key counts; the value records the last hub, so a restored or migrated object stays owned.

Engine Root object Also marked hypershift HostedCluster <namespace>/<cluster> hive ClusterDeployment <cluster>/<cluster> ManagedCluster siteconfig ClusterInstance <cluster>/<cluster> ManagedCluster, through extraAnnotations

Foreign is the first of these that exists without the marker: the root object, else ManagedCluster <cluster>, else for siteconfig ClusterDeployment <cluster>/<cluster>, which SiteConfig would adopt. A marked ManagedCluster without a root, as after a failed ClusterDeployment create, is owned.

Note

Namespace <cluster> and the hypershift secrets are not marked. A same-named Namespace or secret created after a destroy, with no root object left, is deleted by a still-present absent Policy. Only install.namespace is checked for a HostedCluster, so keep HostedCluster names unique on the hub.

items.title: Immutable fields
items.text:
The operators reject changes to these, among others:

Object Immutable HostedCluster services, platform, networking, etcd, issuerURL, controllerAvailabilityPolicy, fips, dns.baseDomain once set. secretEncryption cannot be removed. NodePool clusterName, platform.type, arch, management.upgradeType ClusterDeployment Everything but installAttemptsLimit, powerState, preserveOnDelete and a few others. hive.installConfig changes reach the Secret, not the cluster. On vSphere all of hive.platform.vsphere. ClusterInstance Everything until install completes. After: only extraAnnotations, extraLabels, suppressedManifests, pruneManifests, and adding a node.

Changing one does not change the cluster: present-cluster-<cluster> goes NonCompliant with the API server's message. Revert the value.

  • NodePool upgradeType or arch: add a new pool, remove the old one.
  • Failed SiteConfig install: set state: absent, then build again with the fix.

items.title: Removing a NodePool or host
items.text:
musthave never deletes. Removing an entry only stops managing it.

NodePoolSiteConfig host

Remove the nodePools entry, then:

oc delete nodepool <cluster>-<pool> -n clusters

A pool from a shared layer, like workers in platforms/kubevirt.yaml, cannot be removed from a higher layer (the schema rejects null). Scale it down:

install:
  nodePools:
    workers:
      replicas: 0

Remove the nodes entry, then remove the host from the live object. Changing a host after install needs the same edit.

oc edit clusterinstance <cluster> -n <cluster>

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
Start with the Application for render errors (missing version, credential or required key), then the Policy:

oc get applications.argoproj.io lifecycle-<cluster> -n openshift-gitops -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions}'
Symptom Cause Fix Guard or any step: "<Kind> <cluster> ... not built by lifecycle (no lifecycle.policystk.io/hub annotation); refusing" Imported, built by hand or the console, or built before the marker. Usually hub was added to an imported cluster's fleet file. Remove hub, state, install from the fleet file. If lifecycle built it, annotate the root object. present-credentials NonCompliant, template error Credential Secret missing Create it. Without pullSecret the API rejects the pull secret. Cluster has no SSH key, no error ssh-publickey missing from the credential Add it. hive/siteconfig: present-credentials-<cluster> NonCompliant: because it is being terminated Namespace <cluster> from the last destroy is still terminating Wait until oc get ns <cluster> returns NotFound.

Switching engines

The guard looks for the new engine's root object, not the old one's, so it can miss an engine switch. Destroy before changing engine.

Hive: install failed

present-ready stays NonCompliant, ClusterDeployment shows ProvisionStopped. Read the installer log, fix the values, destroy and build again.

RequirementsMet False with InstallConfigValidationFailed: the install-config and ClusterDeployment regions differ, through hive.clusterDeployment or an edit of hive.platform during install. Revert it.

A cloud key missing from the credential is copied as an empty value and fails the install.

Hive: vSphere credentials rejected

ClusterDeployment AuthenticationFailure True: the hub could not log in to vCenter with <cluster>-creds and <cluster>-certs. Check for a wrong login, a trailing newline, a cacertificate that is not PEM, vCenter on a port other than 443, or no route from the hub. Right after create it can be brief while the trust bundle fills.

RequirementsMet False, "install config does not contain username/password": the credential is missing username or password.

cluster NonCompliant with must specify vSphere vCenter: the hub's Hive predates zonal vSphere support. Upgrade MCE.

Hive: deprovision stuck

absent-destroyed stays NonCompliant; ClusterDeployment shows DeprovisionLaunchError, or the ClusterDeprovision AuthenticationFailure. Fix the keys in <cluster>-creds (or <cluster>-certs on vSphere) directly: the absent Policy no longer copies the credential.

With HiveConfig deleteProtection: enabled:

oc annotate clusterdeployment <cluster> -n <cluster> hive.openshift.io/protected-delete-
SiteConfig: rejected or failed

present-cluster shows a webhook denial, or the ClusterInstance shows Provisioned False:

oc get clusterinstance <cluster> -n <cluster> -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions}'

Check the AgentClusterInstall too. Destroy, fix, build again. A wrong ref, like templateNamespace, can be fixed by creating the missing object.

SiteConfig: cluster never imported

The hub cannot resolve api.<cluster>.<baseDomain>. Add the DNS record where the hub resolves it.

SiteConfig: deletion paused

The ClusterInstance has clusterinstance.siteconfig.open-cluster-management.io/paused: a rendered object (usually a BareMetalHost or the ManagedCluster) was not gone within 30 minutes. Fix what holds it, then remove the annotation.

ManagedCluster stuck Terminating

absent-detached stays NonCompliant. Hosted-mode cleanup waits for the guest; ACM gives up after 5 minutes unreachable. Check:

oc get klusterlet klusterlet-<cluster> -o jsonpath='{.metadata.finalizers}'

If it waits on operator.open-cluster-management.io/klusterlet-hosted-cleanup and the guest will not answer, remove that finalizer.

Agent: Machines stuck Deleting

Machines in <namespace>-<cluster> stay Deleting, PreTerminateDeleteHookSucceeded reports WaitingExternalHook. Remove the hook:

for m in $(oc get machines.cluster.x-k8s.io -n clusters-<cluster> -o name); do
  oc annotate "$m" -n clusters-<cluster> pre-terminate.delete.hook.machine.cluster.x-k8s.io/agentmachine-
done
Agent: stuck reclaiming

After destroy, Agents go to reclaiming while they reboot into discovery. One that cannot ends in UnbindingPendingUserAction: boot it from the discovery ISO by hand. Agents still holding the agent.agent-install.openshift.io/ai-deprovision finalizer block any new cluster that selects them.

items.title: Adding an engine
items.text:
An engine <e> is a component of lifecycle/. templates/policy.yaml renders whichever component install.engine names, so the ApplicationSet and fleet keys do not change.

  1. Add converters/<e>/: objects to create, root.yaml (the root object by identity alone, for destroy and ownership), and its credentials. lookup back every field the engine rejects changes to. End the cleanup converter with include "lifecycle.cleanupManifests".
  2. Add stack.<e> to values.yaml with present and absent Policies following the chains. Set every gate to InformOnly, which ACM keeps inform under a Policy-level enforce. No pruneObjectBehavior: it lets a Policy delete a cluster.
  3. Add <e> to the install.engine enum in values.schema.json, with its keys. POLICY090 fails when the enum and stack keys differ (Rules).
  4. Merge lifecycle.marker into the root object's annotations in the cluster converter, and start every enforced converter but manifests with include "lifecycle.refuse". Add the engine to TestOwnership, a present and an absent fleet file to tools/validator/testdata/clusters/, and an example to Cluster lifecycle.

An engine that upgrades from the hub maps version onto its objects, like hypershift. One that only installs uses version at create and leaves upgrades to upgrade (Upgrades).

items.title: Cluster lifecycle
items.text:
Add hub to a fleet file and that hub builds the cluster. Set state: absent and it destroys it. After import, the same fleet file drives Day-2 (Fleet files).

  1. ApplicationSet policystack-lifecycle creates Application lifecycle-<cluster> for each fleet file naming the hub.
  2. It renders the lifecycle/ chart into Policy present-lifecycle-<cluster>, placed on the hub. For a default-mode Global Hub managed hub, the parent does this (Global Hub).
  3. ACM creates the cluster's objects in order, each step waiting for the last.
  4. ACM imports the finished cluster and the Day-2 ApplicationSet takes over.

The cluster is built when present-lifecycle-<cluster> is Compliant. Only ACM and Argo CD run. Every key and object: Lifecycle reference.

items.title: Pick an engine
items.text:
You want install.engine install.platform Upgraded by OpenShift on AWS, GCP, Azure or vSphere hive upgrade on the cluster OpenShift on bare metal with a BMC siteconfig upgrade on the cluster Hosted control plane, workers as VMs on the hub hypershift (default) KubeVirt The hub Hosted control plane, bare-metal workers hypershift Agent The hub Hosted control plane, workers you boot yourself hypershift None The hub

hypershift runs the control plane as pods on the hub. hive and siteconfig build standalone clusters.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text:
On every hub that builds clusters:

  • ACM 2.16 or later.
  • The hub manages itself (local-cluster label, the default), or is a default-mode Global Hub managed hub with PolicyStack on the global hub.
  • fleet/hubs/<hubName>.yaml exists.
  • hypershift: the hypershift-addon, on by default (oc get managedclusteraddon hypershift-addon -n local-cluster).
  • A credential Secret with pullSecret, ssh-publickey and, for hive, cloud keys (vSphere: username, password, cacertificate). Labels cluster.open-cluster-management.io/credentials= and cluster.open-cluster-management.io/type=<type> show it in the console.

items.title: Examples
items.text:
Copy one, change names and addresses, merge. Values moves shared parts into a layer.

AWSGCPAzurevSphereBare metalKubeVirtAgentNone

Needs a public Route 53 zone for baseDomain and EC2 quota.

oc create namespace hive-credentials
oc create secret generic aws -n hive-credentials \
  --from-literal=aws_access_key_id=<key> --from-literal=aws_secret_access_key=<secret> \
  --from-file=pullSecret=pull-secret.json --from-file=ssh-publickey=id_ed25519.pub

# fleet/ocp-aws.yaml
revision: main
hub: acm-dc1 # (1)!
version: 4.20.8
channel: stable-4.20
install:
  engine: hive
  credential:
    namespace: hive-credentials
    name: aws
  baseDomain: aws.example.com
  hive:
    platform:
      aws:
        region: us-east-2
    installConfig: # (2)!
      controlPlane:
        name: master
        architecture: amd64 # (3)!
        replicas: 3
        platform:
          aws:
            type: m6i.xlarge
      compute:
        - name: worker
          architecture: amd64
          replicas: 3
          platform:
