            aws:
              type: m6i.xlarge
  1. hubName of the hub that builds the cluster.
  2. Any install-config content. Set for you: apiVersion, metadata, baseDomain, platform, pullSecret, and sshKey from the credential.
  3. Keep it, or the install follows the hub node's architecture.

Single node: controlPlane.replicas: 1 with type: m6i.2xlarge, and compute[0].replicas: 0.

Needs a public Cloud DNS zone for baseDomain, a service account with the installer's roles or Owner, and the compute, dns, iam, cloudresourcemanager and serviceusage APIs.

oc create secret generic gcp -n hive-credentials \
  --from-file=osServiceAccount.json=sa-key.json \
  --from-file=pullSecret=pull-secret.json --from-file=ssh-publickey=id_ed25519.pub

# fleet/ocp-gcp.yaml
revision: main
hub: acm-dc1
version: 4.20.8
channel: stable-4.20
install:
  engine: hive
  credential:
    namespace: hive-credentials
    name: gcp
  baseDomain: gcp.example.com
  hive:
    platform:
      gcp:
        projectID: my-project
        region: us-central1
    installConfig:
      controlPlane:
        name: master
        architecture: amd64
        replicas: 3
        platform:
          gcp:
            type: n2-standard-4
      compute:
        - name: worker
          architecture: amd64
          replicas: 3
          platform:
            gcp:
              type: n2-standard-4

Needs an Azure DNS zone for baseDomain in baseDomainResourceGroupName, and a service principal with Contributor and User Access Administrator on the subscription.

cat > sp.json <<EOF
{"subscriptionId":"<sub>","clientId":"<appId>","clientSecret":"<password>","tenantId":"<tenant>"}
EOF
oc create secret generic azure -n hive-credentials \
  --from-file=osServicePrincipal.json=sp.json \
  --from-file=pullSecret=pull-secret.json --from-file=ssh-publickey=id_ed25519.pub

# fleet/ocp-azure.yaml
revision: main
hub: acm-dc1
version: 4.20.8
channel: stable-4.20
install:
  engine: hive
  credential:
    namespace: hive-credentials
    name: azure
  baseDomain: azure.example.com
  hive:
    platform:
      azure:
        region: eastus
        baseDomainResourceGroupName: dns-rg
    installConfig:
      controlPlane:
        name: master
        architecture: amd64
        replicas: 3
        platform:
          azure:
            type: Standard_D8s_v5
      compute:
        - name: worker
          architecture: amd64
          replicas: 3
          platform:
            azure:
              type: Standard_D4s_v5

Needs vCenter and ESXi 7.0.2+, vCenter on port 443, DNS for api.<cluster>.<baseDomain> and *.apps.<cluster>.<baseDomain> pointing at the VIPs, and DHCP on the network unless hosts sets static IPs. Inventory paths are absolute. More than one failure domain needs the openshift-region and openshift-zone tag categories attached to the datacenters and clusters. The hub downloads the RHCOS OVA unless topology.template names one.

cacertificate is the vCenter CA in PEM, from https://<vcenter>/certs/download.zip (certs/lin/*.0). It is required even for a publicly trusted vCenter. Use --from-literal: a trailing newline in the login fails the install.

oc create secret generic vsphere -n hive-credentials \
  --from-literal=username=<user> --from-literal=password=<password> \
  --from-file=cacertificate=vcenter-ca.pem \
  --from-file=pullSecret=pull-secret.json --from-file=ssh-publickey=id_ed25519.pub

# fleet/ocp-vsphere.yaml
revision: main
hub: acm-dc1
version: 4.20.8
channel: stable-4.20
install:
  engine: hive
  credential:
    namespace: hive-credentials
    name: vsphere
  baseDomain: vsphere.example.com
  hive:
    platform:
      vsphere: # (1)!
        apiVIPs: [10.0.10.5]
        ingressVIPs: [10.0.10.6]
        vcenters:
          - server: vcenter.example.com # (2)!
            datacenters: [dc1]
        failureDomains:
          - name: dc1-cl1
            region: dc1
            zone: cl1
            server: vcenter.example.com
            topology:
              datacenter: dc1
              computeCluster: /dc1/host/cl1
              datastore: /dc1/datastore/ds1
              networks: [ocp-vlan10]
    installConfig:
      controlPlane:
        name: master
        architecture: amd64
        replicas: 3
      compute:
        - name: worker
          architecture: amd64
          replicas: 3
      networking:
        machineNetwork:
          - cidr: 10.0.10.0/24 # (3)!
  1. The installer's platform.vsphere, also the ClusterDeployment's infrastructure. Fixed at create.
  2. Every vCenter logs in with the credential. user and password here are refused.
  3. Holds the node IPs and both VIPs.
Static IPs, two failure domains

hosts lists exactly one bootstrap, then one entry per control-plane and compute replica.

vsphere:
  apiVIPs: [10.0.10.5]
  ingressVIPs: [10.0.10.6]
  vcenters:
    - {server: vcenter.example.com, datacenters: [dc1]}
  failureDomains:
    - {name: dc1-cl1, region: dc1, zone: cl1, server: vcenter.example.com,
       topology: {datacenter: dc1, computeCluster: /dc1/host/cl1, datastore: /dc1/datastore/ds1, networks: [ocp-vlan10]}}
    - {name: dc1-cl2, region: dc1, zone: cl2, server: vcenter.example.com,
       topology: {datacenter: dc1, computeCluster: /dc1/host/cl2, datastore: /dc1/datastore/ds2, networks: [ocp-vlan10]}}
  hosts:
    - {role: bootstrap, networkDevice: {ipAddrs: [10.0.10.10/24], gateway: 10.0.10.1, nameservers: [10.0.0.53]}}
    - {role: control-plane, failureDomain: dc1-cl1, networkDevice: {ipAddrs: [10.0.10.11/24], gateway: 10.0.10.1, nameservers: [10.0.0.53]}}
    - {role: control-plane, failureDomain: dc1-cl2, networkDevice: {ipAddrs: [10.0.10.12/24], gateway: 10.0.10.1, nameservers: [10.0.0.53]}}
    - {role: control-plane, failureDomain: dc1-cl1, networkDevice: {ipAddrs: [10.0.10.13/24], gateway: 10.0.10.1, nameservers: [10.0.0.53]}}
    - {role: compute, failureDomain: dc1-cl1, networkDevice: {ipAddrs: [10.0.10.21/24], gateway: 10.0.10.1, nameservers: [10.0.0.53]}}
    - {role: compute, failureDomain: dc1-cl2, networkDevice: {ipAddrs: [10.0.10.22/24], gateway: 10.0.10.1, nameservers: [10.0.0.53]}}
    - {role: compute, failureDomain: dc1-cl1, networkDevice: {ipAddrs: [10.0.10.23/24], gateway: 10.0.10.1, nameservers: [10.0.0.53]}}

Static IPs and Day-2 nodes

With hosts, the installer creates the workers as standalone Machines and leaves the worker MachineSets at 0, drawing addresses from an IPPool. Nothing installs an IPAM controller for it, so Machines from scaling, infra-nodes or storage-nodes wait for an address.

Note

Hive cannot hibernate vSphere clusters: leave powerState unset. After rotating the vCenter password, update the credential and the cluster's kube-system/vsphere-creds.

Needs:

  • stack.acm.config.siteConfig: true in the hub's values layer.
  • Central infrastructure management: AgentServiceConfig agent, and Provisioning provisioning-configuration with watchAllNamespaces: true (and provisioningNetwork: Disabled if the hub has none).
  • Hosts with a Redfish virtual-media BMC the hub reaches. Hosts reach the hub's image service and API.
  • DNS for api.<cluster>.<baseDomain> from hosts and hub. Multi-node adds api-int and *.apps.
oc create namespace bm-credentials
oc create secret generic hostinventory -n bm-credentials \
  --from-file=pullSecret=pull-secret.json --from-file=ssh-publickey=id_ed25519.pub
oc create secret generic bmc -n bm-credentials --from-literal=username=<user> --from-literal=password=<password>

# fleet/sno-edge.yaml
revision: main
hub: acm-dc1
version: 4.20.8
channel: stable-4.20
install:
  engine: siteconfig
  credential:
    namespace: bm-credentials
    name: hostinventory
  baseDomain: edge.example.com
  siteconfig:
    bmcCredential: # (1)!
      namespace: bm-credentials
      name: bmc
    clusterInstance: # (2)!
      clusterType: SNO
      networkType: OVNKubernetes
      machineNetwork:
        - cidr: 10.20.30.0/24
    nodes: # (3)!
      sno-edge.edge.example.com:
        role: master
        bmcAddress: idrac-virtualmedia://10.20.0.11/redfish/v1/Systems/System.Embedded.1 # (4)!
        bootMACAddress: "00:11:22:33:44:55" # (5)!
        rootDeviceHints:
          deviceName: /dev/sda
  1. username and password, used for every node.
  2. Any ClusterInstance spec field.
  3. Keyed by host name. Each entry takes any ClusterInstance node field.
  4. idrac-virtualmedia:// for Dell, redfish-virtualmedia:// otherwise.
  5. Keep the quotes: an unquoted MAC is not read as a string by YAML.
Three nodes

HighlyAvailable, VIPs, one entry per host:

install:
  siteconfig:
    clusterInstance:
      clusterType: HighlyAvailable
      networkType: OVNKubernetes
      machineNetwork:
        - cidr: 10.20.40.0/24
      apiVIPs: [10.20.40.5]
      ingressVIPs: [10.20.40.6]
    nodes:
      m0.bm-ha.dc1.example.com:
        role: master
        bmcAddress: redfish-virtualmedia://10.20.0.21/redfish/v1/Systems/1
        bootMACAddress: "00:11:22:33:44:01"
      m1.bm-ha.dc1.example.com: ...
      m2.bm-ha.dc1.example.com: ...
Image-based install

siteconfig.templates: ibi. Single node only. Needs the multicluster engine image-based-install-operator component and a host preinstalled with a seed image at version.

Needs OpenShift Virtualization and a LoadBalancer implementation such as MetalLB on the hub; the hosted API server is a LoadBalancer Service.

oc create secret generic kubevirt-secret -n open-cluster-management \
  --from-file=pullSecret=pull-secret.json --from-file=ssh-publickey=id_ed25519.pub

# fleet/hcp-kubevirt.yaml
revision: main
hub: acm-dc1
version: 4.20.8
channel: stable-4.20
install:
  platform: KubeVirt # (1)!
  credential:
    namespace: open-cluster-management
    name: kubevirt-secret
  nodePools:
    workers: # (2)!
      replicas: 2
  1. engine defaults to hypershift. Without baseDomain, HyperShift uses the hub's ingress domain.
  2. NodePool hcp-kubevirt-workers, merged over the generated spec.

Needs:

  • An AgentServiceConfig, as for bare metal, and a LoadBalancer implementation, as for KubeVirt.
  • An InfraEnv in agentNamespace, with hosts booted from its ISO, approved, and labeled to match agentLabelSelector.
  • DNS for *.apps.<cluster>.<baseDomain> at the guest ingress. values/clusters/hcp-agent.yaml pins it with the metallb element.
oc create namespace hcp-credentials
oc create secret generic hostinventory -n hcp-credentials \
  --from-file=pullSecret=pull-secret.json --from-file=ssh-publickey=id_ed25519.pub

# fleet/hcp-agent.yaml
revision: main
hub: acm-dc1
version: 4.20.8
channel: stable-4.20
install:
  platform: Agent
  credential:
    namespace: hcp-credentials
    name: hostinventory
  baseDomain: dc1.example.com
  agentNamespace: hardware-inventory
  nodePools:
    workers:
      replicas: 2
      platform:
        agent:
          agentLabelSelector: # (1)!
            matchLabels:
              example.com/cluster: hcp-agent
  1. A pool without a selector claims any free Agent in agentNamespace.

No machines are created: you boot each worker from the NodePool's Ignition. For VMs or hosts ACM cannot provision. Needs the Agent credential, a hub LoadBalancer, and DNS for *.apps.<cluster>.<baseDomain> at the workers (router on host ports 80/443).

# fleet/hcp-none.yaml
revision: main
hub: acm-dc1
version: 4.20.8
channel: stable-4.20
install:
  platform: None
  credential:
    namespace: hcp-credentials
    name: hostinventory
  baseDomain: dc1.example.com
  nodePools:
    workers: {}

Add a worker once the HostedCluster is up:

# Ignition pointer config with the ignition server URL, token and CA
oc get secret -n clusters-hcp-none -o name | grep user-data-hcp-none-workers \
  | xargs oc get -n clusters-hcp-none -o jsonpath='{.data.value}' | base64 -d > worker.ign
# Boot RHCOS with worker.ign as Ignition or cloud user data, then approve its CSRs twice,
# a minute apart: client, then serving certificate
oc extract secret/hcp-none-admin-kubeconfig -n clusters --to=- > hcp-none.kubeconfig
oc --kubeconfig hcp-none.kubeconfig get csr -o name | xargs oc --kubeconfig hcp-none.kubeconfig adm certificate approve

Workers on AWS

The default service network 172.31.0.0/16 is the AWS default VPC range. Set hostedCluster.spec.networking.serviceNetwork to another range at create. A single worker also needs hostedCluster.spec.infrastructureAvailabilityPolicy: SingleReplica.

items.title: Fleet keys
items.text:
hub, state, version, channel and install are listed in Fleet files. version is required, state defaults to present, and install takes the Install keys.

The cluster name is the fleet file name: a DNS label of at most 30 characters, so every element fits (lifecycle alone allows 38, Naming limits).

Warning

Most install keys are fixed at create (Immutable fields). Changing one later turns the Policy NonCompliant. It never rebuilds the cluster.

items.title: Values
items.text:
Same values cascade as Day-2, starting from lifecycle/values.yaml. The fleet file's install ranks above every layer.

Shipped layers:

Layer Sets values/platforms/aws.yaml engine: hive, credential hive-credentials/aws, 3+3 m6i.xlarge, networking values/platforms/vmware.yaml engine: hive, credential hive-credentials/vsphere, 3+3 amd64 at installer default size values/platforms/baremetal.yaml engine: siteconfig, credentials bm-credentials/hostinventory and bm-credentials/bmc, networkType values/platforms/kubevirt.yaml platform: KubeVirt, credential open-cluster-management/kubevirt-secret, 2 workers values/platforms/agent.yaml platform: Agent, credential hcp-credentials/hostinventory, agentNamespace: hardware-inventory

The AWS example with its layer:

# fleet/ocp-aws.yaml
revision: main
hub: acm-dc1
version: 4.20.8
channel: stable-4.20
valueFiles:
  - platforms/aws.yaml
install:
  baseDomain: aws.example.com
  hive:
    platform:
      aws:
        region: us-east-2

version and channel belong only in the fleet file. values/clusters/<cluster>.yaml may hold both install and stack.

Shared layers

Maps merge, lists replace (Merge rules): installConfig.compute in the fleet file replaces the layer's list. Changing a fixed-at-create key like baseDomain in a layer turns every existing cluster reading it NonCompliant.

items.title: Watching a build
items.text:
oc get policy -n pstack present-lifecycle-<cluster>             # Compliant = built
oc get configurationpolicy -n local-cluster | grep <cluster>    # each step; -n <managed-hub> in default mode
oc get applications.argoproj.io lifecycle-<cluster> -n openshift-gitops -o jsonpath='{.status.conditions}'   # render errors
Engine Progress Typical time hive oc get clusterdeployment -n <cluster>oc logs -f -n <cluster> -l hive.openshift.io/install=true -c installer 45 min on AWS siteconfig oc get clusterinstance,bmh,agentclusterinstall,agent -n <cluster> 1 h single node hypershift oc get hostedcluster,nodepool -n clusters

Every step is in Policy chains.

items.title: Upgrades
items.text:
Bump version, and channel on a minor bump (Upgrades):

 # fleet/hcp-kubevirt.yaml
-version: 4.20.8
-channel: stable-4.20
+version: 4.21.2
+channel: stable-4.21
Engine How hive, siteconfig On the cluster by upgrade, like imported clusters. The hub keeps the install release image; Hive and SiteConfig reject changes to it. hypershift From the hub. With channel, waits until version is in status.version.availableUpdates; without, moves at once. A version below the control plane's desired version is never applied. NodePools follow once the control plane's newest Completed version is version. KubeVirt pools replace VMs; others upgrade in place. Disconnected, channel needs install.hostedCluster.spec.updateService pointing at your OSUS, or the bump waits forever (Disconnected).

During a hypershift upgrade, present-lifecycle-<cluster> is NonCompliant until the control plane and every NodePool reach version. A held downgrade, such as a reverted bump after the control plane moved, keeps it NonCompliant until the fleet file catches up. Clusters install from the -multi payload, so they are multi-architecture.

Minor upgrade blocked by ClusterVersionUpgradeable=False

Force it with the release image:

install:
  hostedCluster:
    metadata:
      annotations:
        hypershift.openshift.io/force-upgrade-to: quay.io/openshift-release-dev/ocp-release:4.21.2-multi

items.title: Destroy
items.text:
Set state: absent and merge:

 # fleet/ocp-aws.yaml
 revision: main
 hub: acm-dc1
+state: absent

The hub detaches the cluster from ACM, deletes it, waits until it is gone, then deletes its secrets and install.manifests. Detaching drops the Day-2 Applications and Policies without pruning the cluster. When the Policy is Compliant, delete the fleet file and values/clusters/<cluster>.yaml:

oc get policy -n pstack absent-lifecycle-<cluster>    # Compliant = gone

Warning

Deleting the fleet file before absent-lifecycle-<cluster> is Compliant abandons the cluster mid-destroy.

ACS

Before re-creating a cluster under the same name, delete it in ACS (Re-register a cluster, step 1).

Engine Left behind hive Nothing. Hive deprovisions the cloud resources or VMs, usually within 20 minutes. vSphere: the DNS records you created. siteconfig Hosts still running, disks not wiped. Power off or reuse. hypershift Agent Agents return to the InfraEnv for the next cluster. hypershift None Your workers and their DNS. Delete them.

items.title: Abandon
items.text:
Delete the fleet file or its hub key: Application lifecycle-<cluster> and its Policies go, the cluster keeps running unmanaged. Deleting the ApplicationSets does this for every cluster the hub built; helm uninstall policystack keeps them (Install PolicyStack). Restore the file or key with the same install to re-adopt.

Changing hub

Moving a cluster between hubs is not supported. Changing hub abandons it on the old hub, and the new hub builds a second, same-named cluster unless the root object is already there with its marker. Destroy it on the old hub first. ACS: run steps 2-3 of Re-register a cluster after the move.

Clusters built before the ownership marker

Lifecycle acts only on a root object carrying lifecycle.policystk.io/hub (Ownership). A cluster built before the marker existed fails the guard and runs unmanaged, nothing deleted, until annotated once:

oc annotate hostedcluster <cluster> -n <install.namespace> lifecycle.policystk.io/hub=<hubName>    # hypershift
oc annotate clusterdeployment <cluster> -n <cluster> lifecycle.policystk.io/hub=<hubName>         # hive
oc annotate clusterinstance <cluster> -n <cluster> lifecycle.policystk.io/hub=<hubName>           # siteconfig
Hub disaster recovery

ACM backup leaves out PolicyStack's ApplicationSets and their Applications (velero.io/exclude-from-backup), so a passive hub builds nothing. Do not install PolicyStack on it before takeover. To take over:

  1. Run the ACM activation restore (veleroManagedClustersBackupName: latest). ClusterDeployments, ClusterInstances and ManagedClusters come back with their annotations.
  2. hypershift: restore the HostedClusters with the HCP OADP procedure. ACM backup does not include them, and without them the hub builds new, empty control planes.
  3. Install PolicyStack with the old hub's hubName. No fleet edits: the restored root objects carry the marker, so the new hub owns them.

items.title: Policies
items.text: Elements render ACM objects with the policy-library chart. Its README is the field reference. PolicyStack fixes three inputs: the values key, the release name, and the cluster selector.

items.title: Element values
items.text:
An element reads stack.<key>, where <key> is the camelCase form of name in its Chart.yaml: metallb reads stack.metallb, user-monitoring reads stack.userMonitoring. One file in the values cascade can configure many elements:

values/clusters/nonprod-west-1.yaml (excerpt)
stack:
  metallb:
    enabled: true        # (1)!
    toggles:
      addressing: true   # (2)!
  userMonitoring:
    enabled: true
    config:
      prometheus:
        retention: 72h
  1. Nothing in the element renders until this is true.
  2. Overrides enabled on the entry named addressing. See Toggles.

Charts also read the top-level policyNamespace, selector and placement.

Note

In an element's values.yaml, a key that doesn't match the chart name renders nothing (POLICY090). In a cascade file, a stack key or toggle that names no element or entry is reported as POLICY035.

items.title: Rendered objects
items.text:
The release name is the Application name, <element>-<cluster> (Applications). Below, <policy>, <set> and <name> are the name of a policies[], policySets[] or template entry, or the key of an operatorPolicies entry.

Object Name Rendered when Policy <policy>-<release> Enabled, and at least one enabled template names it in policyRef. ConfigurationPolicy, CertificatePolicy <policy>-<name> Enabled, and its policyRef Policy renders. Embedded in that Policy. OperatorPolicy <policy>-<name> Same as above. Adds <policy>-<name>-ns (operator namespace, omitted for mustnothave) and <policy>-<name>-status (inform check that the CSV reached Succeeded). PolicySet <set>-<release> Enabled, and policies is not empty. Members resolve to <policy>-<release>. Placement <release> disablePlacements is not true. PlacementBinding <release> disablePlacements is not true and there is something to bind: the Policies, or the PolicySets when usePolicySetsPlacements is true.

Everything except templates lives on the hub in policyNamespace (pstack, root values.yaml). Templates have no namespace; ACM creates them in the cluster's namespace on the managed cluster. The chart ignores policies[].namespace, although its README lists it.

Render metallb for nonprod-west-1 from the repo root. baseline.yaml stands in for the injected selector (Validation).

helm dependency update stack/metallb
helm template metallb-nonprod-west-1 stack/metallb \
  -f values.yaml \
  -f values/environments/nonprod.yaml \
  -f values/datacenters/dc2.yaml \
  -f values/clusters/nonprod-west-1.yaml \
  -f tools/validator/testdata/baseline.yaml

addressing is toggled on; quota stays off and renders nothing:

Placement         metallb-nonprod-west-1
PlacementBinding  metallb-nonprod-west-1
Policy            install-metallb-nonprod-west-1
  OperatorPolicy        install-metallb
  ConfigurationPolicy   install-metallb-ns
  ConfigurationPolicy   install-metallb-status
Policy            config-metallb-nonprod-west-1
  ConfigurationPolicy   config-metallb-instance
Policy            addressing-metallb-nonprod-west-1
  ConfigurationPolicy   addressing-pools
  ConfigurationPolicy   addressing-l2
  ConfigurationPolicy   addressing-bgp
  ConfigurationPolicy   addressing-peers

items.title: Placement
items.text:
The injected selector (Injected values) becomes one In expression on the name label, so each Placement selects only its own cluster:

Placement metallb-nonprod-west-1
spec:
  predicates:
  - requiredClusterSelector:
      labelSelector:
        matchExpressions:
        - key: name
          operator: In
          values:
          - nonprod-west-1
  tolerations: # (1)!
  - key: cluster.open-cluster-management.io/unreachable
    operator: Exists
  - key: cluster.open-cluster-management.io/unavailable
    operator: Exists
  1. Chart default. Policies stay bound while the cluster is disconnected.

A top-level placement: key in any cascade file merges into that spec (Placement overview). A Placement only sees ManagedClusterSets bound to its namespace; the install chart binds global into policyNamespace (Install PolicyStack).

Lifecycle chart

lifecycle/ Policies build clusters on a hub, so its selector is an In expression on the hub's name (Lifecycle generator). The local-cluster Exists default in lifecycle/values.yaml only serves helm lint and the validator.

Every lifecycle release lands on the hub, where template names must be unique across all Policies. The chart sets suffixTemplateNames and templates are named <policy>-<name>-<cluster>, such as present-credentials-hcp-agent.

items.title: Naming limits
items.text:
ACM copies each Policy into the cluster's namespace on the hub, named and labelled <policyNamespace>.<policy>-<release>. Label values max out at 63 characters.

pstack.addressing-metallb-nonprod-west-1
│      │          │       └ cluster
│      │          └ element
│      └ policy
└ policyNamespace (7 with the dot, leaves 56)

Policy, element and cluster names share those 56 characters. Keep policy names short.

Entry Replicated name Characters install pstack.install-metallb-nonprod-west-1 37 config pstack.config-metallb-nonprod-west-1 36 addressing pstack.addressing-metallb-nonprod-west-1 40

POLICY001 holds <policyNamespace>.<policy>-<release>, <policyNamespace>.<set>-<release> and every template name to 63 characters (Rules).

30-character budget

Every element fits a cluster or hub name of 30 characters; most fit 35. CI checks every policy in each element's values.yaml, enabled or not, against fixture cluster name-budget-30-characters-long.

Lifecycle: the longest name is pstack.present-lifecycle-<cluster>, 25 characters plus the cluster, so cluster names can reach 38. The longest template, present-credentials-<cluster>, fits at that length.

items.title: Library reference
items.text: Chart README: Policy dependencies, Depending on another component, Toggles, Raw object templates, Placement overview.

items.title: Rolling out changes
items.text: A cluster runs what Git holds at the revision its fleet file pins. To ship a change, commit it and point fleet files at a revision that has it.

items.title: Onboarding a cluster
items.text:
1. Import the cluster into ACM. The GitOpsCluster adds it to Argo CD (Install PolicyStack).
  2. Add values/clusters/<cluster>.yaml with the elements this cluster runs beyond its other layers.

  3. PR fleet/<cluster>.yaml to the default branch:

    # fleet/prod-east-1.yaml
revision: main # (1)!
valueFiles: # (2)!
  - environments/prod.yaml
  - datacenters/dc1.yaml
  - platforms/aws.yaml
    1. Branch, tag or SHA.
    2. Under values/, lowest precedence first. values/clusters/prod-east-1.yaml is added last (Order).

Within about 6 minutes there is one Application per element, named <element>-<cluster>. An element no layer enables still gets an Application, with no resources.

oc get applications.argoproj.io -n openshift-gitops | grep prod-east-1

Name both files exactly like the ManagedCluster

A misnamed values file is skipped silently (Missing files). Commit it at the revision the fleet file pins (with the fleet file PR when that is the default branch), or the first render leaves it out and can briefly enable an element it turns off.

For a cluster the hub builds, skip step 1 and add hub, version and install to the fleet file (Cluster lifecycle). The hub itself uses fleet/hubs/<hubName>.yaml and values/clusters/<hubName>.yaml (The hub).

items.title: Promoting and rolling back
items.text:
A branch revision picks up every push. A tag or SHA changes only when revision does. Promote with a PR; its Render Diff comment shows the Policy changes.

 # fleet/prod-east-1.yaml
-revision: v1.4.0
+revision: v1.5.0

Roll back with git revert, or a PR that sets the old revision. Both need the usual fleet/ review (Protection).

  • Application names don't include the revision, so Argo CD updates the same Policies in place.
  • The Placement matches only the cluster's name label, so policies stay bound during the sync.
  • An element added at the new revision gets an Application. One missing loses it and its Policies (Removing an element).

items.title: Dry run
items.text:
Set global.remediationAction: inform in any layer (Global keys). Every Policy for clusters reading that layer, lifecycle included, reports instead of enforcing. To preview a revision on one cluster, add this to its file at the revision it reads and remove it once the Policies look right:

# values/clusters/prod-east-1.yaml
global:
  remediationAction: inform # (1)!
  1. enforce is rejected. Remove the key to go back to each template's own setting. InformOnly gates stay inform either way.

On a branch pin, add the key in the PR with the change. A tag or SHA pin reads the cluster file at the pin, so a key added at HEAD never reaches the cluster. To promote v1.4.0 to v1.5.0:

  1. Commit the key on a branch from v1.5.0 and push it.
  2. Pin that commit's SHA and check the Policies.
  3. Pin v1.5.0. It lacks the key, so enforcement resumes.

Note

Inform undoes nothing already applied. A Policy waiting on another stays Pending, so on a new cluster only the start of each dependency chain reports.

Dry run stops enforcement, not removal

Argo CD still prunes and self-heals, and the resources finalizer still deletes the Policies of an element the revision drops (Removing an element). A dropped or renamed Policy whose template sets pruneObjectBehavior is deleted with its last enforce spec, so its objects go too (What happens on the managed cluster). Check the "removed" counts in the PR's Render Diff first.

items.title: Disabling an element
items.text:
Set enabled: false in a layer that outranks every layer enabling it (Order). environments/prod.yaml enables dns; to turn it off on one cluster:

# values/clusters/prod-east-1.yaml
stack:
  dns:
    enabled: false
  remediations:
    toggles:
      samples: false # (1)!
  1. A toggle turns off one entry of an element.

The element renders nothing, sync prunes it from the hub (allowEmpty is set), and ACM removes its policies from the cluster (What happens on the managed cluster). A failed render prunes nothing: the Application shows ComparisonError / Unknown and the Policies stay.

items.title: Removing an element
items.text:
Delete stack/<element>. When a cluster's revision no longer has it, the ApplicationSet deletes the Application and the resources finalizer deletes its Policies, PolicySets, Placement and PlacementBinding. Clusters pinned to older revisions keep it until their pin moves.

Applications are also deleted when:

Trigger See Fleet file deleted Offboarding a cluster Cluster detached (GitOpsCluster deletes its Argo CD secret) Argo CD secret or its clusterID label disappears Pausing removals ApplicationSet deleted Teardown

A fleet file that doesn't parse, or a missing revision, deletes nothing (Revision).

items.title: Offboarding a cluster
items.text:
Delete the fleet file in a PR. Its Applications and Policies go with it. If the file sets hub, choose what happens to the cluster:

DestroyAbandon

Set state: absent, wait for Policy absent-lifecycle-<cluster> to be Compliant, then delete the file (Destroy). Nothing is pruned on the cluster: its governance add-on is already gone.

Delete the file, or remove hub. The hub deletes the lifecycle Policies and the cluster keeps running, unmanaged (Abandon). Deleting the file also deletes the Day-2 Policies, and templates with pruneObjectBehavior prune on the still-attached cluster.

Warning

Don't reuse a cluster name while its fleet file exists. The new cluster gets the old configuration.

items.title: What happens on the managed cluster
items.text:
The policy goes away; what it created stays unless the template sets pruneObjectBehavior, is enforce, and that setting reached the cluster before the removal.

Case Effect None (default) or inform Everything stays, patched fields included. DeleteIfCreated Deletes objects this policy instance created. A recreated policy, or a re-imported cluster, adopts them and won't. DeleteAll Deletes every object the template manages, pre-existing ones too. OperatorPolicy Operator, CSV, CRDs and CRs stay. A pinned or None Subscription stays on manual approval, so upgrades stop. An unpinned one keeps upgrading. Gatekeeper constraints and templates Deleted. Cluster detached, or governance add-on removed Nothing pruned. Cluster disconnected Prunes on reconnect.

Prune deletes live objects

Set pruneObjectBehavior in its own commit and remove the policy only after it reached the cluster. Renaming an element, policy, template or hubName deletes and recreates objects, which with prune set happens on the managed cluster too.

  • POLICY033 rejects prune on a template with any dependency (waitForOperator, extraDependencies, the policy's dependencies, or a place after another template/policy under orderManifests/orderPolicies). ACM deletes a template while a dependency is unmet, such as during an operator upgrade, and prune would delete its objects (Validation).
  • Keep the Placement's default tolerations. With placement.tolerations: [], a disconnected cluster drops out and loses its policies.

items.title: Pausing removals
items.text:
Do this before an ACM upgrade or work on Argo CD cluster secrets. The ACM 2.17 upgrade can swap a cluster's secret for a renamed one and briefly drop its Applications and Policies.

# pause deletes; creates and updates continue
oc patch applicationset policystack -n openshift-gitops --type merge \
  -p '{"spec":{"syncPolicy":{"applicationsSync":"create-update"}}}'

# resume (helm upgrade does not remove it)
oc patch applicationset policystack -n openshift-gitops --type json \
  -p '[{"op":"remove","path":"/spec/syncPolicy/applicationsSync"}]'

items.title: Operator upgrades
items.text:
Each operatorPolicies entry renders an OperatorPolicy named after its key (Operator Policy Options).

upgradeApproval versions When enforced Automatic empty OLM installs every upgrade the channel offers. Automatic listed Approves an InstallPlan only for a CSV in versions or subscription.startingCSV. None either Approves the first install only, never an upgrade.
  • ACM rejects Manual and subscription.installPlanApproval.
  • Inform approves nothing; it flags an installed CSV missing from a non-empty versions.
  • versions holds exact CSV names, no wildcards. Comma-separated names need ACM 2.14+, templates 2.13+.
  • The hub's ACM and GitOps follow the same rules once their elements are on (Hand the operators to PolicyStack).

Elements ship unpinned. operatorPolicies is a map, so a layer sets only what it changes (Merge rules):

# values/environments/prod.yaml
stack:
  metallb:
    operatorPolicies:
      metallb: # (1)!
        versions:
          - <installed CSV> # (2)!
        subscription:
          startingCSV: <installed CSV> # (3)!
  1. Must be a key the element defines. A new key fails POLICY032 (Validation) and the render.
  2. oc get csv -n metallb-system on the managed cluster.
  3. Without it, a fresh cluster resolves the channel head, which the pin blocks. Omit it when the pin is the head.

To bump, watch the OperatorPolicy status for an InstallPlan to update to [<csv>]. OLM picks that CSV from the upgrade graph; the policy only approves or holds it.

  1. Add the new CSV next to the old one. Promote cluster by cluster (Promoting and rolling back).
  2. Once all clusters run it, drop the old CSV, move startingCSV, and promote again.

Swapping old for new in one change makes every cluster NonCompliant until it upgrades.

Goal Set on the key Result Unpin versions: [] in a higher layer, or delete the pin Follows the channel Stop managing enabled: false or toggles.<key>: false (never null) Stays installed Uninstall complianceType: mustnothave Deletes Subscription, CSV, and an unused OperatorGroup. Keeps CRDs and namespace (Removing an operator)

Stop managing and Uninstall both fail the render unless entries naming the key in waitForOperator are turned off in the same layer.

# values/clusters/prod-east-1.yaml: uninstall metallb
stack:
  metallb:
    toggles:
      metallb-instance: false # (1)!
    operatorPolicies:
      metallb:
        complianceType: mustnothave # (2)!
  1. The instance waits on metallb, so it goes off in the same layer.
  2. removalBehavior changes what is deleted.

items.title: Upgrades
items.text:
Set version in the cluster's fleet file and merge. On a minor bump, change channel too.

 # fleet/prod-east-1.yaml
 revision: v3.0.0
-version: 4.20.8
+version: 4.20.12
 channel: stable-4.20
Key Effect version OpenShift release x.y.z the cluster runs. Unset, nothing upgrades it. Required on a cluster a hub builds. channel Update channel. Unset, the cluster's channel is left alone.

Both keys live only in the fleet file (fleet/<cluster>.yaml, or fleet/hubs/<hubName>.yaml for a hub). The validator rejects them in a values layer (POLICY034), so the clusters a merge upgrades are exactly the fleet files it changes, and the Render Diff lists each one.

Note

version must be a full x.y.z. Unquoted, version: 4.20 is the number 4.2; the validator rejects any value YAML reads as a number (POLICY050).

A wave is one commit that bumps several fleet files:

 # fleet/nonprod-west-1.yaml
-version: 4.20.8
+version: 4.21.2
-channel: stable-4.20
+channel: stable-4.21
 # fleet/prod-east-1.yaml
-version: 4.20.8
+version: 4.21.2
-channel: stable-4.20
+channel: stable-4.21

items.title: Who upgrades what
items.text:
Each field has one writer.

Built by a hub with the hypershift engineAny other cluster, hubs included

lifecycle-<cluster> on the hub writes HostedCluster spec.release and spec.channel, then each NodePool's release once the control plane completes. Downgrades are never attempted. See Cluster lifecycle.

The upgrade element is inert on the guest (Infrastructure controlPlaneTopology: External), since HyperShift owns its ClusterVersion.

The upgrade element on the cluster writes ClusterVersion spec.channel, spec.desiredUpdate and spec.upstream.

An imported hosted cluster is the exception: the element is inert on any HyperShift guest, so PolicyStack does not upgrade it.

items.title: upgrade element
items.text:
Enabled by default. Renders nothing until the fleet file sets version or channel, or a layer sets config.upstream.

Template Policy (renders when) Mode Does channel-pin channel-upgrade-<cluster> (channel or config.upstream set) enforce Sets ClusterVersion spec.channel and spec.upstream, each only when set. Not held by the guard. upgrade-guard upgrade-upgrade-<cluster> (version set) InformOnly NonCompliant unless version is in availableUpdates, is already the desired version, or is at or below the current version. The message lists the ClusterVersion conditions holding it. upgrade-trigger same enforce After the guard is Compliant, sets desiredUpdate.version, only while version is newer than current and no update is progressing. Clears image and force left by oc/console; leaves architecture. upgrade-progress same InformOnly NonCompliant until the cluster has completed version. The message lists the ClusterVersion conditions.
  • A version the update service does not offer is held at the guard.
  • Downgrades are never attempted.

Brownfield clusters

The CVO ignores desiredUpdate.version while image is set, and oc adm upgrade and the console leave the running image there. The trigger therefore clears image and force: a pending oc/console request that has not started is replaced while the fleet version is newer, and a hand-set force does not survive.

channel-pin sets spec.upstream from stack.upgrade.config.upstream. Empty (the default) leaves the cluster's value alone; a cluster with none uses the public graph. On a local OpenShift Update Service, set it in a values layer:

# values/datacenters/dc1.yaml
stack:
  upgrade:
    config:
      upstream: https://osus.example.internal/api/upgrades_info/v1/graph

Warning

Removing the key leaves the last URL on the cluster. To go back to the public graph, set upstream: https://api.openshift.com/api/upgrades_info/v1/graph. toggles.channel gates upstream too.

Watch it:

# on the hub: each template's latest message
oc get policy -n prod-east-1 pstack.upgrade-upgrade-prod-east-1 \
  -o jsonpath='{range .status.details[*]}{.templateMeta.name}{": "}{.history[0].message}{"\n"}{end}'
oc get clusterversion version -o jsonpath='{.status.history[0]}'    # on the cluster
Migrating from config.targetVersion / config.channel

Both keys are gone; the render fails while any layer sets them. In the commit that bumps revision, delete them from the values layer and set version and channel in the fleet file:

 # values/clusters/prod-east-1.yaml
 stack:
   upgrade:
-    config:
-      targetVersion: 4.20.12
-      channel: stable-4.20

 # fleet/prod-east-1.yaml
+version: 4.20.12
+channel: stable-4.20

items.title: Pausing
items.text:
Turn a toggle off in any layer the cluster reads:

# values/clusters/prod-east-1.yaml
stack:
  upgrade:
    toggles:
      upgrade: false # (1)!
      channel: false # (2)!
  1. Deletes upgrade-upgrade-<cluster>. An update already started on the cluster keeps running.
  2. Stops managing the channel and upstream.

A hosted cluster is paused by leaving version where it is.

Why not ClusterCurator or TALM?

ClusterCurator runs an upgrade as a one-shot Job: a failure is not retried, and a Policy owning the ClusterCurator cannot tell a finished upgrade from a new one. TALM's ClusterGroupUpgrade is also one-shot and needs its own inform policies. ClusterVersion is declarative, so a Policy can keep enforcing it.

items.title: Validation
items.text: tools/validator renders every element in stack/ for each fixture cluster, building the values cascade like the ApplicationSet (Order), and checks sources and output. Needs Go and the Helm version CI pins (Policy Validate). kubeconform is optional; without it POLICY080 is skipped.

items.title: Running it
items.text:
The CI commands, from the repo root:

make -C tools/validator lint test build # (1)!
tools/validator/bin/policystack-validator --repo-root . \
  --extra-values tools/validator/testdata/baseline.yaml \
  --include-sample-element --skip POLICY080,POLICY081 # (2)!
for p in tools/validator/testdata/profiles/*.yaml; do # (3)!
  tools/validator/bin/policystack-validator --repo-root . --only RENDER000,POLICY081 \
    --extra-values "tools/validator/testdata/baseline.yaml,$p"
done
  1. Format check, vet, Go tests, build.
  2. Validates the fixtures. Policy Validate explains the skips.
  3. Evaluates every converter's ACM templates, see ACM templates.

--extra-values files override the whole cascade, except in lifecycle/, which ships its own selector. baseline.yaml supplies the selector the ApplicationSet normally injects (Placement). Without it helm template fails on any enabled element:

tools/validator/testdata/baseline.yaml
selector:
  matchExpressions:
    - key: name
      operator: Exists

Note

helm dependency update runs unless charts/ already holds <name>-<version>.tgz for every dependency. Bumping policy-library to an unpublished version fails the fetch, and RENDER000 reports the element unrendered.

items.title: Fixtures
items.text:
tools/validator/testdata/clusters holds example fleet files. The file name is the cluster name: hubs/acm-dc1.yaml renders as acm-dc1 and reads values/clusters/acm-dc1.yaml. A fixture that sets hub also renders lifecycle/ as lifecycle-<cluster>, with the fixture itself appended to the cascade (Cluster lifecycle).

Fixture list Fixture Covers prod-east-1, nonprod-west-1 Imported managed clusters, version and channel hubs/acm-dc1 The hub the lifecycle fixtures name hcp-kubevirt, hcp-agent HyperShift hive-aws Hive on AWS hive-vsphere Hive on vSphere, one failure domain, DHCP sno-edge SiteConfig single-node hcp-retired, hive-retired, sno-retired state: absent name-budget-30-characters-long The 30-character name every element must fit (Naming limits)

items.title: ACM templates
items.text:
Helm treats escaped ACM templates ({{ "{{" }} ... {{ "}}" }}) as strings. POLICY081 resolves them with go-template-utils, the library ACM uses, against an empty cluster. The hub pass also holds the operator-owned objects hub templates index into (hubObjects in acmtemplates.go), so their absence is not reported:

  1. {{hub ... hub}} as the policy propagator does. Lookups stay in the policy namespace unless the policy sets hubTemplateOptions.serviceAccountName.
  2. {{ ... }} as the config-policy-controller does: object-templates-raw whole, each object-templates entry separately with skipObject.

It fails on an undefined function (in any branch), a failed call such as index on nil, a hub lookup outside the policy namespace, a kind the fake cluster does not serve (misspelled kind or apiVersion), and output with <no value> or an object missing apiVersion/kind.

A missing object is not a failure: on a real cluster another policy or operator creates it. Evaluation stops there, so branches that need existing objects are parsed but not run. Guard such lookups with dig and skipObject:

stack/acs/converters/acs-console-link.yaml
href: '{{ "{{" }} $host := (lookup "route.openshift.io/v1" "Route" "{{ .Parameters.namespace }}" "central").spec.host {{ "}}" }}{{ "{{" }} skipObject (not $host) {{ "}}" }}https://{{ "{{" }} $host {{ "}}" }}'

Looking up a new kind

Add it to kinds in tools/validator/internal/acmtemplates/acmtemplates.go.

Fixtures leave most elements off, so CI evaluates against tools/validator/testdata/profiles, which turn every element and toggle on. Add a new element or toggle to all-on.yaml, or to variants.yaml if it conflicts with one there. TestProfileCoverage fails until every converter with ACM templates renders under some profile.

tools/validator/testdata/profiles/all-on.yaml
stack:
  acs:
    enabled: true
    toggles:
      console: true

Profiles enable toggles without their input maps, so POLICY082 fires there; CI runs only RENDER000 and POLICY081 on them. A change to a lifecycle converter's ACM template needs a test case in tools/validator/internal/acmtemplates, which resolves them against fake hub objects.

items.title: Rules
items.text: ID Severity What it catches POLICY001 error Policy/PolicySet ACM-replicated name <ns>.<name>-<release> > 63 chars; ConfigurationPolicy/OperatorPolicy/CertificatePolicy metadata.name (<parent>-<sub>) > 63 chars POLICY002 error Duplicate rendered metadata.name WITHIN one element POLICY003 error Two different elements render a policy-template with the same name. ACM requires template names to be unique across every Policy on a cluster, so policies[].name: install + configPolicies[].name: ns-monitoring in two elements is rejected on-cluster with "Template name must be unique". Covers toggled-off entries and the -ns/-status templates an operatorPolicy generates POLICY010 error policyRef points to nonexistent or disabled parent policy POLICY011 error dependency reference that can never be satisfied: unknown dependencies/extraDependencies target, unknown element:, element: on a template kind, waitForOperator naming no enabled operator, or a target policy policy-library never emits (no enabled sub-policy attached) POLICY020 error templateNames[].name has no matching converters/<name>.yaml; <name> may contain /, as in hypershift/ready POLICY021 warning Converter file not referenced by any templateNames[].name POLICY022 error A converter reads a top-level config key missing from the element's values.yaml, which renders as null: .Values.stack.<el>.config.<key>, from $ too, or $v.<key> with $v bound to .Values.stack.<el>.config. Only Helm actions count, not escaped ACM templates. Nested keys are not checked POLICY030 error/warning Invalid enum: severity / remediationAction / complianceType / upgradeApproval (None or Automatic). configPolicies[].remediationAction also takes InformOnly, any case. In operatorPolicies entries also: subscription.installPlanApproval set, a versions entry or subscription.startingCSV that is not a valid CSV name (templated entries skipped, comma-separated versions entries split), and a name: key, which is ignored (warning) POLICY031 error/warning values keys policy-library never reads: enable: (element renders nothing) and defaultPolicy: (metadata silently dropped) are errors; default.severity/.remediationAction/.disabled are warnings. Also flags rawTemplate: true with more than one templateNames entry, and operatorPolicies as a list (policy-library 3.x needs a map) POLICY032 error/warning stack.<el>.operatorPolicies in a values layer: a key the element's values.yaml does not define, a list, or any POLICY030 operator problem. Reported once per layer file POLICY033 error/warning configPolicies[].pruneObjectBehavior other than None: an invalid value, an effective remediationAction other than enforce (a policy-level value overrides the template's unless it is InformOnly), or any dependency (waitForOperator, extraDependencies, parent dependencies, orderManifests unless first template, orderPolicies unless first Policy), since ACM deletes the template whenever the dependency is unmet. DeleteAll is a warning POLICY034 error Top-level version or channel in a values layer: only the fleet file sets them. Reported once per layer file POLICY035 error A key in the root values.yaml or a file under values/ that nothing reads: an unknown top-level or global key, a stack key that names no element, an element key policy-library's schema rejects (reported here at the layer; RENDER000 reports it once per element at its values.yaml), a toggles key that names no entry of the element or of the layer's own lists, or a top-level config key missing from the element's values.yaml. Checks every file, used by a fleet file or not POLICY036 error A configPolicies or operatorPolicies entry whose remediationAction differs (case-insensitive) from a set policies[].remediationAction of its parent. ACM applies the Policy-level action to every template, so an inform mustnothave gate under an enforce Policy deletes. InformOnly is skipped: ACM keeps it inform. An unset configPolicies action counts as the chart default, inform. Covers toggled-off entries POLICY040 error policySets[].policies[] references a name not in policies[] POLICY050 error Invalid fleet file: YAML error, unknown key, missing or empty revision, revision, hub, state, version, channel or valueFiles entry Argo CD reads as a number or boolean, valueFiles entry that is null, listed twice, or not a file under values/; version that is not x.y.z, install.version; empty hub, version or channel, hub with no hubs/<hub>.yaml, hub naming the cluster itself, hub in a hub file, state other than present/absent, install that is not a map, state or install without hub, or a cluster that sets hub whose name is not a DNS label POLICY060 warning policy-library version drift across element Chart.yaml files POLICY070 error helm lint non-zero POLICY080 error kubeconform schema check on rendered manifests POLICY081 error An escaped ACM template ACM would fail to resolve, resolved hub then managed on an empty cluster: an undefined function in any branch, a failed call such as index on nil, a hub lookup outside the policy namespace without hubTemplateOptions.serviceAccountName, a kind discovery does not serve, or output with <no value> or an object without apiVersion/kind. A missing object is not a failure. Findings name the sub-policy without its cluster suffix and carry no cluster, so a broken template reports once POLICY082 error A rendered Policy whose every template is a ConfigurationPolicy with no objects (object-templates-raw empty or [], or no object-templates). ACM reports it Compliant without checking anything; policy-library renders [] when a raw converter's input map is empty. A Policy with only some empty templates passes POLICY090 error Chart.yaml name → camelCase mismatch with single key under stack:. For a chart whose values.schema.json has an install.engine enum (lifecycle/), a stack: key that is not an engine or an engine with no stack: key. Every other check then runs on each engine's component, and each fixture renders the one its install.engine selects POLICY091 error An element name equal to another's, or starting with another's followed by -. Release names join element and cluster with -, so a on cluster b-c and a-b on cluster c would share one Application and its Policies. lifecycle/ takes part, which reserves lifecycle RENDER000 error helm template failed, or helm dependency update did. A chart whose dependencies were not fetched is not rendered, since Helm would use any charts/ archive of the dependency, whatever its version. Reported once per chart

items.title: Values cascade
items.text: Each Application renders its element chart with an ordered list of values files picked by the cluster's fleet file. Later files win. The list is built in appset.yaml.

items.title: Order
items.text:
Managed clusterHubLifecycle 
# fleet/prod-east-1.yaml
revision: main
channel: stable-4.20
valueFiles:
  - environments/prod.yaml
  - datacenters/dc1.yaml
  - platforms/aws.yaml

Application infra-nodes-prod-east-1, lowest precedence first:

valueFiles:
  - values.yaml                             # (1)!
  - ../../values.yaml                       # (2)!
  - ../../values/environments/prod.yaml     # (3)!
  - ../../values/datacenters/dc1.yaml
  - ../../values/platforms/aws.yaml
  - ../../values/clusters/prod-east-1.yaml  # (4)!
valuesObject:                               # (5)!
  channel: "stable-4.20"
  selectedName: prod-east-1
  selectedId: <clusterID label>
  selector:                                 # (6)!
    matchExpressions:
      name: {key: name, operator: In, values: ["prod-east-1"]}
  1. Element defaults. Paths are relative to stack/<element>.
  2. Repo root, shared by every element. Sets policyNamespace.
  3. One per valueFiles entry, in list order. Nothing sorts them.
  4. Always last. Named after the ManagedCluster.
  5. Injected values. Ranks above every file.
  6. Targets this one cluster. For the hub, values holds local-cluster, not hubName.

The hub reads fleet/hubs/<hubName>.yaml, and hubName replaces local-cluster in the Application name and cluster values file (The hub).

# Application nfd-acm-dc1
valueFiles:
  - values.yaml
  - ../../values.yaml
  - ../../values/environments/prod.yaml
  - ../../values/datacenters/dc1.yaml
  - ../../values/platforms/baremetal.yaml
  - ../../values/acm/acm-dc1.yaml
  - ../../values/clusters/acm-dc1.yaml   # never clusters/local-cluster.yaml

Same files, relative to lifecycle/: values.yaml, ../values.yaml, ../values/<entry>, ../values/clusters/<cluster>.yaml. valuesObject holds the fleet file's hub, state, version, channel and install (Values). Elements ignore install, so one cluster values file holds both:

# values/clusters/hcp-agent.yaml
install: ...   # lifecycle/ builds the cluster
stack: ...     # elements configure it once imported

Merged stack.infraNodes for prod-east-1, trimmed:

enabled: true                 # clusters/prod-east-1.yaml
toggles:
  aws: true                   # platforms/aws.yaml
  workloads: false            # element default
config:
  replicas: 1                 # clusters/prod-east-1.yaml, default 3
  zones:                      # clusters/prod-east-1.yaml, replaces default []
    - us-east-1a
    - us-east-1b
    - us-east-1c
  maxPods: 250                # element default

items.title: Missing files
items.text:
ignoreMissingValueFiles: true skips any listed file absent at the cluster's revision. Add a values/clusters/ file only for clusters that change something.

A skipped file raises no error

The Application syncs from the remaining layers. Elements default to off, so it looks like an element that never turns on.

Cause Validator Typo in a valueFiles entry POLICY050 Entry for a file the cluster's pinned revision lacks Fleet pin check Cluster values file name differs from the ManagedCluster name Fleet pin check (warning)

Compare the Application's files with the repo at the cluster's revision:

oc get applications.argoproj.io infra-nodes-prod-east-1 -n openshift-gitops \
  -o jsonpath='{.spec.source.helm.valueFiles}'

items.title: Merge rules
items.text:
Maps merge key by key. Lists replace.

Map: set only what changesList: restate everything 
# values/clusters/nonprod-west-1.yaml
stack:
  userMonitoring:
    config:
      prometheus:
        retention: 72h   # other prometheus keys keep their defaults
        storage: 20Gi

# values/datacenters/dc2.yaml
stack:
  remediations:
    config:
      allowedRegistries:
        - mirror.dc2.example.com:8443
        - quay.io                    # the defaults, restated
        - registry.redhat.io
        - image-registry.openshift-image-registry.svc:5000

policies and configPolicies are lists. Change them through maps instead:

Change Key One policy on or off toggles, e.g. stack.remediations.toggles.registries A converter setting config (Conventions) One operator field stack.metallb.operatorPolicies.metallb.versions. versions is a list and replaces (Operator upgrades)

items.title: Schema
items.text:
Each element aliases policy-library as stack in its Chart.yaml, so Helm checks the merged stack key against the library's values.schema.json after every layer:

Error: values don't meet the specifications of the schema(s) in the following chart(s):
stack:
- at '/certManager': additional properties 'enabeld' not allowed

Argo CD shows a ComparisonError and does not sync or prune. Every element validates the whole stack key, so one typo in a shared layer fails every Application reading it.

The validator's POLICY035 checks every file under values/ for what the schema misses (Validation):

Mistake Caught by Unknown key in an element (enabeld) schema, POLICY035 Wrong type in an element schema Unknown top-level or global key POLICY035 Unknown element (stack.certManagr) POLICY035 Toggle that names no entry POLICY035 Top-level config key absent from the element's values.yaml POLICY035 Deeper config keys nothing

Warning

Never set skipSchemaValidation on the ApplicationSet.

items.title: Global keys
items.text:
global applies from any layer: one cluster, a site or an environment.

Key Effect remediationAction inform makes every Policy, lifecycle included, report instead of enforce (Dry run). enforce is rejected. catalogSources Maps a CatalogSource name to its replacement for every operator (Disconnected clusters) 
global:
  remediationAction: inform
  catalogSources:
    redhat-operators: cs-redhat-operator-index-v4-20

items.title: Example files
items.text:
values/ configures the example clusters. Any file under values/ can be listed. Every element but upgrade ships enabled: false, so the layer that should run an element turns it on. upgrade acts only on the fleet file's version and channel (Upgrades).

What each example file holds File Holds environments/prod.yaml Prod baseline: cert-manager, External Secrets, Compliance Operator, remediations, DNS environments/nonprod.yaml Nothing datacenters/dc1.yaml install.baseDomain datacenters/dc2.yaml Registry allowlist through the dc2 mirror platforms/aws.yaml Node toggles: clone the worker MachineSet. install: Hive platforms/vmware.yaml Node toggles: clone each MachineSet per failure domain. install: Hive platforms/baremetal.yaml Node toggles: no MachineSets, label nodes. install: SiteConfig platforms/kubevirt.yaml install only: KubeVirt, 2-node workers pool platforms/agent.yaml install only: Agent, no default NodePool tenants/payments.yaml GitOps operator plus a payments team Argo CD acm/acm-dc1.yaml Hub ACM and GitOps, commented out (why) clusters/acm-dc1.yaml Hub elements, and which are off and why clusters/prod-east-1.yaml Infra nodes, machine health, user monitoring clusters/hcp-agent.yaml install: hosted control plane service publishing. stack: guest MetalLB pool clusters/nonprod-west-1.yaml Registry enforcement, MetalLB pool, user monitoring clusters/aws-prod.yaml ODF to Loki chain. Rename to the real ManagedCluster name first

CI renders with the fleet files in tools/validator/testdata/clusters/. None lists payments.yaml and no cluster is named aws-prod, so CI reads those only when a file in fleet/ uses them.

items.title: CI Workflows
items.text:
Workflow (.github/workflows/) Trigger Fails when Policy Validate (validate.yml) Changes to stack/, lifecycle/, install/, values/, values.yaml, fleet/, tools/sample-element/, tools/validator/ Validator error, bad fleet pin, broken install chart, failing test Documentation Check (docs-check.yml) Changes to stack/ or the doc generator An element README is stale Render Diff (render-diff.yml) PRs to the default branch changing stack/, lifecycle/, values/, values.yaml, fleet/ Not a gate Update Documentation (docs-update.yml) update-docs label on a PR Not a gate Documentation Site (docs-site.yml) Every PR and main push A relative link, anchor or snippet does not resolve

Checks run on PRs and pushes to main. A new push to a PR cancels its running checks. Policy Validate, Documentation Check and Documentation Site can also be started from the Actions tab.

items.title: Policy Validate
items.text:
Findings are annotated on the PR at the file and line to fix. Errors fail the job, warnings only annotate.

# Every validator run also gets --repo-root .; steps 2 and 4 also get --extra-values tools/validator/testdata/baseline.yaml
make -C tools/validator lint build                                                  # (1)!
policystack-validator --github --include-sample-element --skip POLICY080,POLICY081  # (2)!
policystack-validator --github --extra-values "tools/validator/testdata/baseline.yaml,$profile" --only RENDER000,POLICY081 # (3)!
policystack-validator --github --fixtures-dir fleet --skip POLICY080                # (4)!
# fleet pin check, install chart check (below)
make -C tools/validator test                                                        # (5)!
  1. gofmt, vet, build. Go version comes from tools/validator/go.mod.
  2. Fixture clusters plus tools/sample-element/. POLICY080 is always skipped: it ignores every kind the chart emits.
  3. Once per file in tools/validator/testdata/profiles/. They turn every element on, so every converter's ACM templates are evaluated (ACM templates). Runs even if step 2 failed.
  4. Only when fleet/*.yaml or fleet/hubs/*.yaml exist. Renders the PR's tree, not each file's revision (Render Diff does that).
  5. Last, so a failing test does not hide the annotations.

Fleet pin check. Each revision must be a tag, branch or commit SHA (5 to 40 hex characters) whose commit contains what the file uses, including every valueFiles entry. A pin to the PR's base branch is checked against the merge commit. A values/clusters/<name>.yaml with no fleet/<name>.yaml or fleet/hubs/<name>.yaml is a warning, since a tag-pinned cluster's file lands first (Onboarding).

fleet/prod-east-1.yaml
revision: v1.4.0  # (1)!
hub: acm-dc1      # (2)!
version: 4.20.8   # (3)!
  1. v1.4.0 must contain stack/ and each valueFiles entry. A typo or a branch like gh-pages fails.
  2. Also needs lifecycle/converters/hypershift/.
  3. version or channel also needs an upgrade element that reads them.

Warning

A pinned branch deleted after merge is not caught, and stops Argo CD generating Applications for every cluster. See Revision.

Install chart check. Runs even if an earlier step failed. helm lint install passes, an empty hubName or gitRepo fails the install, policyNamespace matches between install/values.yaml and values.yaml, and install/operators renders the ACM and GitOps operators plus a MultiClusterHub (Installation).

Note

HELM_VERSION pins Helm in validate.yml and render-diff.yml. Keep them equal, on the major the hub's Argo CD bundles. Dependabot does not update it.

Run it locally: Validation.

items.title: Render Diff
items.text:
Comments on the PR with what the merge changes in each fleet/ cluster's rendered Policies. No fleet files or no change means no comment.

### Fleet render: 3 cluster(s) change

> [!WARNING]
> `edge-3` pins `v1.4`, which is not a tag, branch or commit. Merging stops Argo CD from generating Applications for every cluster until it is fixed.

| Cluster | Revision | Changes |
|---|---|---|
| `prod-east-1` | `main` | user-monitoring: 1 Policy changed |
| `nonprod-west-1` | `v1.0.0` → `main` | metallb: **render failed** |
| `edge-2` | new at `main` | 6 elements, 21 objects added |

Each cluster gets a collapsed diff per element below the table, or the Helm error. render fixed means it failed on the base branch and renders now. An element that fails the same way on both sides is not listed. A cluster added or removed shows totals only.

Each fleet file renders at its own revision, before and after the merge (.github/scripts/render-diff.sh). A cluster pinned to main or HEAD shows the PR. One pinned to a tag changes only when its pin moves.

Limits

  • Comments stop near 60,000 characters. The full patch is the run's render-diff.patch artifact.
  • Fork and Dependabot PRs have a read-only token and get the result in the job summary.
  • About 30 seconds per distinct commit rendered.

items.text:
Builds docs/ with zensical build --strict. On main, a second job publishes site/ to the gh-pages branch as a single commit, using a GitHub App. The site is unversioned: for an older revision, read docs/ at that revision on GitHub.

Absolute links, nav in zensical.toml, and snippet content. Keep the rules section of tools/validator/README.md free of relative links, and restart serve after editing it.
